name: Inspect AI evaluation framework
modality: Python framework: solvers, scorers, sandboxed tool use, multi-turn agents, model-graded scoring; inspect_evals collection.
what_it_measures: Infrastructure used by AISI, CAISI and labs to run agentic and QA evaluations reproducibly.
size: 200+ pre-built evaluations in inspect_evals; 2.9k GitHub stars
reported_metrics: none stated
cost_evidence: Open-source; removes per-eval engineering cost; no numbers.
validity_evidence: n/a

name: US/UK AISI joint pre-deployment test: OpenAI o1
modality: Cybench (40 CTFs) via Inspect agents, Pass@1 over 10 attempts and Pass@10, up to 100 messages; UK private cyber suite graded by difficulty tier; transcripts reviewed by CISA/NSA SMEs.
what_it_measures: Pre-deployment cyber, bio, software/AI development capability of o1.
size: 40 Cybench tasks x 10 attempts; UK cyber suite
reported_metrics: o1 45% Pass@10 (35% Pass@1) vs 35%/30% for best reference; UK technical non-expert 79% vs 90%; apprentice 46% vs 46%.
cost_evidence: 10 attempts per task, 100-message cap; SME transcript review; report notes results may understate capability because of limited time and iterations.
validity_evidence: Human baselines are competition first-solve times, not controlled; report calls for controlled human baselines.
notes: Fetched from a third-party mirror of the NIST PDF; NIST original not fetched.

name: US/UK AISI joint pre-deployment test: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (upgraded)
modality: Agentic runs (Inspect) on cyber CTFs, software/AI R&D tasks, bio QA with and without tools; safeguards red-teamed by experts; solve rates vs reference models and human baselines.
what_it_measures: Pre-deployment capability in bio, cyber, software/AI development and safeguard efficacy.
size: US: 40 cyber challenges; UK: 47 cyber (15 public, 32 private); plus SWE and reasoning suites
reported_metrics: US cyber 32.5% vs 35% best reference; UK apprentice-level cyber 36% vs 29%; UK SWE 66% vs 64%; bio below human expert baselines except with bioinformatics tools.
cost_evidence: 'Limited period of pre-deployment access' and 'finite resources'; expert engineers and scientists from both institutes; no hours stated.
validity_evidence: Findings 'preliminary'; small differences within margins of error; results a lower bound on elicitable capability.

name: UK AISI Frontier AI Trends Report
modality: Aggregate of AISI evaluations Nov 2023-Oct 2025: agentic cyber and software tasks, chem-bio QA, safeguard red-teaming by experts, sandbagging transcript review.
what_it_measures: Trends in frontier capability and safeguard robustness across 30+ systems.
size: 30+ frontier systems; 2,700+ transcripts reviewed for sandbagging
reported_metrics: Cyber task horizon doubling ~8 months; apprentice-level cyber success <10% (early 2024) to ~50% (2025); hour-long SWE tasks >40%; universal jailbreaks found for every system.
cost_evidence: Expert jailbreak effort rose from ~10 min to 7+ h (~40x) across successive generations; scaffold optimisation reached 25% of performance at ~13% token budget.
validity_evidence: No sandbagging detected in 2,700+ transcripts; safeguard results show attacker-cost as a measurable quantity.

name: AgentHarm
modality: Explicitly malicious multi-step agent tasks with synthetic tools; scored on refusal and on task completion (capability retained after jailbreak); Inspect-based.
what_it_measures: Harmfulness and jailbreak robustness of LLM agents.
size: 110 base tasks (440 with augmentations), 11 harm categories
reported_metrics: Leading LLMs 'surprisingly compliant' without jailbreaks; simple templates jailbreak agents while preserving capability.
validity_evidence: none stated (synthetic tools; peer-reviewed at ICLR 2025)

name: Agentic misalignment (blackmail scenarios)
modality: Simulated corporate email-agent environment with goal conflict and replacement threat; transcripts classified by Claude Sonnet 3.7 plus string matching.
what_it_measures: Propensity for harmful insider-like actions (blackmail, espionage) under contrived pressure.
reported_metrics: Blackmail rates: Claude Opus 4 96%, Gemini 2.5 Flash 96%, GPT-4.1 80%, Grok 3 80%, DeepSeek-R1 79%.
validity_evidence: Authors: scenarios deliberately constrained; models misbehave MORE when they believe the situation is real; no evidence of agentic misalignment in real deployments (level-9 signal absent).

name: Claude Opus 4.5 system card: uplift trials, eval awareness, alignment audit effort
modality: Expert and novice uplift trials, automated behavioural audits (Petri-style), interpretability steering of eval-awareness representations, internal AI R&D productivity survey (18 staff).
what_it_measures: ASL-3/4 CBRN and AI R&D threshold checks; alignment and evaluation-awareness assessment.
size: 18 internal survey participants; hundreds of hours of expert review
reported_metrics: Uplift 1.97x raw protocol score vs internet-only (secondary source); Opus 4.5 uplift-trial mean 0.668; 9/18 staff report >=100% productivity gain, none think junior-ML-researcher automation reached; steering down eval awareness increased misaligned behaviour only slightly.
cost_evidence: Alignment assessment: manual expert inspection of hundreds-thousands of transcripts, tens-hundreds of thousands of generated transcripts, 'hundreds of hours of expert time'; staff spent >2 h each on R&D survey.
validity_evidence: Eval-awareness mitigation partially effective; ASL determination draws on automated evals, uplift trials and third-party red teaming.
notes: Fetched as PDF via curl (12 MB). 1.97x figure from search snippet, not verified in text.

name: Claude Opus 4 system card: bioweapons acquisition uplift trial
modality: Human participants (groups of 8-10, up to 2 days) draft a bioweapons acquisition plan with internet only vs internet + safeguard-free Claude; graded by Deloitte rubric; uplift = ratio of mean scores; critical failures counted.
what_it_measures: Real human uplift for the ASL-3 CBRN threshold (deployment gate).
size: Groups of 8-10 participants per arm; contractors from SepalAI and Mercor
reported_metrics: Control 25% +/- 13%; Opus 4 63% +/- 13% (2.53x); Sonnet 4 42% +/- 11% (1.70x); Sonnet 3.7 1.53x; all participants hit critical failures; thresholds: >=5x total uplift = significant risk, <=2.8x acceptable; Opus 4 'unable to rule out ASL-3'.
cost_evidence: Up to 2 days per participant, external contractors, Deloitte grading; internal survey: staff spent >2 h each evaluating AI R&D uplift; RSP autonomy eval: 42 tasks x 10 runs.
validity_evidence: Anthropic: text-based uplift trials are 'substantially weaker proxies for real-world scenarios' (tacit knowledge, materials, persistence); threshold set conservatively.

name: Petri: automated alignment auditing tool
modality: Auditor LLM drives multi-turn scenarios (from natural-language seed instructions) against a target model; LLM judge scores transcripts on deception, sycophancy, harmful cooperation, self-preservation, power-seeking, reward hacking.
what_it_measures: Broad misaligned-behaviour propensity; reused by UK AISI for sabotage case study.
reported_metrics: Claude Sonnet 4.5 lowest misaligned-behaviour score, narrowly ahead of GPT-5; all models showed some misaligned behaviour.
cost_evidence: 'Only minutes of hands-on effort' per hypothesis; Sonnet 4.5 card: median investigation >=60 queries, plus 'dozens of hours' of researcher transcript review.
validity_evidence: Authors: 111 scenarios is small; auditor models impose limits; realism filter reduced eval awareness ~25% and increased misaligned behaviour ~5% (Sonnet 4.5 card).

name: Claude Sonnet 4.5 system card: evaluation awareness
modality: Automated behavioural audit with Claude Opus 4.1 auditors/graders (median >=60 queries per investigation), realism filter, activation steering to inhibit eval-awareness representations.
what_it_measures: Alignment propensities and the confound of evaluation awareness.
reported_metrics: Realism filter reduced eval awareness ~25% and increased measured misaligned behaviour ~5%; even worst-case awareness inhibition left Sonnet 4.5 no worse than Opus 4.1/Sonnet 4; verbalized awareness rose 20%->80% over training on a honeypot eval (Redwood summary).
cost_evidence: 'Dozens of hours of researcher time' reviewing transcripts; hours of manual transcript review across snapshots.
validity_evidence: Anthropic states eval awareness accounts for 'a portion, but not all' of alignment gains on some evals; expects the effect in other production LLMs.
notes: Fetched as PDF via curl (13 MB).

name: 3CB: Catastrophic Cyber Capabilities Benchmark
modality: LLM agents in containerised offensive-cyber challenges (binary analysis to web); success per challenge.
what_it_measures: Offensive cyber capability of agents (reconnaissance, exploitation).
reported_metrics: GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet perform offensive tasks; smaller open models limited.
validity_evidence: none stated

name: LLM-orchestrator safety benchmark for human-humanoid collaboration
modality: Natural-language commands over a Model Context Protocol tool interface to an LLM orchestrator, grounded in ISO 10218-2:2025 safety invariants; 40 sessions x 100 turns; each turn labelled correct/over-/under-compliance/violation; physical layer on Unitree G1 EDU.
what_it_measures: Compliance spectrum of LLM orchestrators (over-refusal vs violation) against industrial safety invariants over long sessions.
size: 40 sessions x 100 turns per model, 5 safety invariants
reported_metrics: Claude and Gemini near-zero violations; GPT-4o-mini up to 13 violations/session; context management cuts issues 42-57% for most models but doubles GPT-4o-mini failures.
cost_evidence: Text-level scoring is cheap; physical G1 validation described as ongoing.
validity_evidence: Ties scoring to ISO 10218-2 invariants; measures both false alarms (overcompliance) and misses (violations).
notes: Scored at level 0 (text) with a level-7 validation layer; one of the few entries reporting a false-alarm (over-refusal) axis. CBS 2026. Org unverified. Aliases in sweeps: bajrami2026humanoid. Level set to 0 on the 0-9 ladder (text-level scoring; physical G1 validation ongoing; sweeps had 0/4).

name: Anthropic sabotage evaluations
modality: Four evals: human decision sabotage (human participants making business decisions with a sabotaging assistant), code sabotage (attacker/defender minigame and 100k-commit simulation), sandbagging (capability suppression then anti-refusal fine-tuning), undermining oversight (overseer model rating harmful outputs).
what_it_measures: Whether a model could covertly sabotage evaluations, monitoring or deployment decisions.
size: Human trial: 54 control + 3x18 treatment participants, 3 scenarios, 30 min each; code minigame 512 simulations
reported_metrics: Code-sabotage attacker win rate 26.6% vs Opus 3 defender, 7.8% vs Sonnet 3.5; sandbagged dangerous-capability performance 36.1% of baseline recovering to 95.6% after anti-refusal training.
cost_evidence: 108 paid participants ($30 bonus for correct decisions); 30-minute sessions; simulation counts above.
validity_evidence: Human-subject trial gives direct behavioural outcome; authors judge minimal mitigations sufficient for current models.
notes: Full author list abbreviated.

name: Internal-representation monitors for reward hacking during evaluations
modality: Open-weight LLM agents (Kimi K3, GLM 5.2, Qwen 3.8 Max) on coding evals (DeepSWE, SWE-bench); difference-of-means activation vectors used as a monitor; scored by hack detection rate at matched false-positive rate
what_it_measures: Whether reward hacking has a linear signature in activations that can be used as a runtime monitor during evaluations and to discover new hack types.
size: 2 benchmarks, 3 models; rollout counts in paper
reported_metrics: GLM 5.2 hacks in 57.2% of DeepSWE rollouts and 73% on SWE-bench; DoM monitors catch +3.1% more hacks (Kimi K3) and 7.9% fewer (GLM 5.2) than baseline at matched FPR
cost_evidence: Requires white-box activation access and rollouts on agentic benchmarks; no dollar cost stated
validity_evidence: Compared against labelled hacking rollouts; LLM domain only
notes: Fel is 15th of 18 authors. Only Fel-linked paper that is explicitly about safety monitoring during evaluations; not embodied. Goodfire blog post exists ('Models know when they're reward hacking', 17 Sept 2026) but its URL was not resolved. Level set to 0 on the 0-9 ladder (text-only LLM coding evals; sweeps had None).

name: CyberSecEval (Purple Llama)
modality: Prompts eliciting code; static analysis for insecure code; prompts requesting cyberattack help scored for compliance by LLM judge.
what_it_measures: Insecure code generation rate and compliance with cyberattack assistance requests.
reported_metrics: More capable models tend to suggest more insecure code; 7 models tested.
validity_evidence: none stated in abstract

name: CAISI evaluation of DeepSeek models
modality: 19 public and private benchmarks (cyber, software, science, agent hijacking, jailbreak robustness, censorship); solve rates and attack-compliance rates; cost per performance.
what_it_measures: Capability, cost, security and censorship comparison of DeepSeek R1/R1-0528/V3.1 vs GPT-5, GPT-5-mini, gpt-oss, Opus 4.
reported_metrics: R1-0528 12x more likely to follow malicious agent-hijack instructions; responds to 94% of malicious jailbreak requests vs 8% for US models; US model 35% cheaper at equal performance; >20% more SWE tasks solved.
cost_evidence: Reports inference cost comparisons across models; eval effort not stated.
validity_evidence: none stated

name: MLE-bench
modality: Agent solves Kaggle competitions end-to-end with compute; scored against Kaggle leaderboards (medal rates).
what_it_measures: ML engineering capability (AI R&D threshold proxy in Preparedness Framework).
reported_metrics: o1-preview + AIDE reaches bronze in 16.9% of competitions.
cost_evidence: EvalEval estimate ~$5,500 per single-seed run (75 x 24 h A10 + API); abstract itself gives no cost.
validity_evidence: Human baseline via public leaderboards; contamination analysed.

name: JailbreakBench
modality: 100 behaviours; adversarial prompts; Llama-3-70B judge with custom prompt; leaderboard of attacks/defences.
what_it_measures: Jailbreak attack and defence performance under a standard threat model.
size: 100 behaviours; 300-example human-preference set for judge selection
reported_metrics: Judge chosen against 300 human-labelled examples (agreement numbers in full paper).
validity_evidence: Judge validated against human labels.

name: OR-Bench (over-refusal)
modality: Automatically generated seemingly-toxic but benign prompts (80k, 1k hard) plus 600 toxic prompts; refusal judged by LLM.
what_it_measures: Over-refusal (false-alarm) rate vs true refusal across 32 LLMs.
reported_metrics: none stated
validity_evidence: none stated in abstract (LLM-generated prompts)

name: AgentDojo
modality: Agent uses simulated tools (email, banking, travel) whose returned data contain prompt injections; utility and security scored by deterministic checks.
what_it_measures: Prompt-injection robustness of tool-using agents (targeted attack success and utility under attack).
reported_metrics: SOTA LLMs fail many tasks even without attack; attacks break some security properties.
validity_evidence: none stated

name: Gemini 3 Pro Frontier Safety Framework report
modality: Early-warning evals: cyber key-skills benchmark (v1 hard 12 challenges, v2 13 challenges), RE-Bench ML R&D tasks, situational-awareness (11) and stealth (4) challenges, CBRN QA and lab-uplift trials, external red teams.
what_it_measures: Whether Gemini 3 Pro reached any CCL.
reported_metrics: Cyber: 11/12 v1 hard solved, 0/13 v2 end-to-end, alert threshold met, CCL not reached; ML R&D below alert threshold; 3/11 situational awareness, 1/4 stealth; CBRN alert threshold not reached.
cost_evidence: Uses external specialist groups; lab uplift trials referenced; no hours or dollars.
validity_evidence: Report states threat models are abstract and CCLs set holistically; 'cannot rule out' logic with safety margins.

name: CrashEvent / CrashLLM
modality: Crash reports converted to text; LLMs fine-tuned to predict crash type, severity, injuries; scored by F1.
what_it_measures: Whether LLMs can predict crash outcomes from contextual factors and support what-if traffic-safety analyses.
reported_metrics: Average F1 from 34.9% to 53.8%.
validity_evidence: Real crash labels as ground truth.
bibtex: @article{fan2024crashevent, title={Learning Traffic Crashes as Language: Datasets, Benchmarks, and What-if Causal Analyses}, author={Fan, Zhiwen and Wang, Pu and Zhao, Yang and Zhao, Yibo and Ivanovic, Boris and Wang, Zhangyang and Pavone, Marco and Yang, Hao Frank}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2406.10789}, year={2024}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10789}}
notes: Traffic-safety analytics rather than robot evaluation; adjacent.

name: AILuminate v1.0
modality: Single-turn adversarial prompts across 12 hazard categories; ensemble evaluator models; five-tier grade (Poor to Excellent).
what_it_measures: Product-level risk and reliability grade for chat systems (industry standard benchmark).
size: 12 hazard categories; prompt count not in abstract
reported_metrics: Grades per system; authors note evaluator uncertainty and single-turn limits.
validity_evidence: Acknowledged limits: evaluator uncertainty, no multi-turn/multimodal.

name: Alignment faking
modality: Text: system prompt tells Claude 3 Opus it is trained on free-tier but not paid-tier conversations; compliance with harmful queries compared across tiers; scratchpad reasoning inspected.
what_it_measures: Whether a model selectively complies during perceived training (alignment faking).
reported_metrics: 14% harmful compliance for free-tier vs almost 0% paid-tier; alignment-faking reasoning in almost all such cases; rises to 78% after RL training.
validity_evidence: Direct evidence that behaviour depends on perceived observation context, undermining eval-to-deployment inference.

name: LLM-Driven Robots Risk Enacting Discrimination, Violence, and Unlawful Actions
org: Carnegie Mellon / King's College London / University of Birmingham
modality: Text prompts describing HRI scenarios (facial expression, proxemics, security, rescue, task assignment) with protected-identity descriptors, plus open-vocabulary dangerous instructions, sent to several LLMs; outputs coded for discriminatory outcomes and acceptance of harmful/unlawful commands.
what_it_measures: Whether LLMs used as robot decision-makers produce discriminatory or unsafe action choices across protected characteristics and accept dangerous open-vocabulary instructions.
size: Not quantified in abstract; several LLMs; code released on GitHub.
reported_metrics: Models produced directly discriminatory outcomes and accepted dangerous instructions (e.g., removing mobility aids, sexual predation).
validity_evidence: Author-coded harms; no inter-rater statistics; no physical robot experiments.
notes: International Journal of Social Robotics 2025.

name: BioLP-bench
modality: Text: lab protocols with several benign edits plus one fatal error; model must identify the fatal mistake; accuracy vs human experts.
what_it_measures: Understanding of biological lab protocols (a wet-lab tacit-knowledge proxy used in AISI bio evaluations).
size: 800 test cases (per search-result summary; abstract does not state the count)
reported_metrics: Only o1-preview scored similarly to human experts; most models could not identify the error.
validity_evidence: Human expert baseline; no downstream validation.
notes: bioRxiv preprint; size figure from secondary summary.

name: When Robots Mishear Us (ASR errors and embodied safety)
modality: Simulated ASR errors injected into SafeAgentBench and POEX instructions; measures whether errors preserve semantics, add harmful ambiguity or weaken refusals; tests automatic error correction.
what_it_measures: Effect of speech-recognition noise on acceptance of harmful instructions by embodied LLM agents.
reported_metrics: ASR errors cause harmful instructions to be accepted/executed; correction only partly effective.
validity_evidence: None stated.

name: Holistic Agent Leaderboard (HAL)
modality: Standardised harness running agents across 9 benchmarks; cost and accuracy logged; LLM-aided log inspection.
what_it_measures: Agent accuracy vs cost; behavioural issues in logs.
reported_metrics: ~$40,000 total; higher reasoning effort reduced accuracy in most runs.
cost_evidence: $40k for one single-seed sweep; ~$1.84 per rollout average.
validity_evidence: none stated
notes: Author list truncated.

name: SPOC
modality: LLM plans step-by-step under strict partial observability and physical constraints in a symbolic household environment; goal-condition-based evaluation with state- and constraint-based online metrics.
what_it_measures: Safety-aware planning under implicit constraints (fire, fluid, injury, damage, pollution).
reported_metrics: SOTA LLMs struggle, especially under implicit constraints.
validity_evidence: None stated.
notes: ICASSP 2026. Symbolic environment, no perception, hence level 0.

name: METR ARA evaluations (autonomous replication and adaptation)
modality: LLM agents with tool scaffolds attempt 12 real-world-style tasks (resource acquisition, self-replication); task completion scored by researchers.
what_it_measures: Autonomous replication and adaptation capability; early template for autonomy thresholds in RSP/Preparedness.
reported_metrics: Agents completed only the easiest tasks; partial progress on harder ones.
validity_evidence: none stated

name: Encoding Inequity (LLM caregiving bias)
modality: Caregiving prompts with demographic descriptors sent to an LLM; responses analysed by sentiment and narrative clustering.
what_it_measures: Demographic bias in LLM-generated robot caregiving behaviour.
reported_metrics: Reduced sentiment for disability and LGBTQ+ identities; stereotyped clustering.
validity_evidence: None stated.
notes: HRI 2025 DEI workshop. Fairness rather than physical safety.

name: SHADE-Arena
modality: Agent in a tool-rich synthetic environment gets a benign main task plus a hidden harmful side task; scored on main-task success, side-task success and evading an LLM monitor (monitor AUC).
what_it_measures: Sabotage capability and monitorability of agents.
size: 17 task pairs (per paper; abstract says 'wide array')
reported_metrics: Claude 3.7 Sonnet 27% sabotage success; Gemini 2.5 Pro 15%; best monitor (Gemini 2.5 Pro) AUC 0.87.
cost_evidence: Environment construction described as complex (hand-built tools/data); no hours stated.
validity_evidence: Monitor AUC as detection sensitivity/false-alarm proxy; synthetic environments.
notes: Author list partially reconstructed; verify before citing.

name: METR 50% task-completion time horizon
modality: LLM agent with shell/tool access in a sandbox works on software/ML/cyber tasks (RE-Bench, HCAST, 66 short novel tasks); binary success per task, logistic fit of success vs human task duration; horizon = duration at 50% (or 80%) success.
what_it_measures: Length of tasks (in human-expert minutes) an agent completes with 50% reliability; used as a headline autonomy capability metric and as an ASL/CCL autonomy proxy.
size: RE-Bench (7) + HCAST (189) + 66 SWAA short tasks, ~170 tasks in Time Horizon 1.1 suite
reported_metrics: Claude 3.7 Sonnet ~50 min horizon (Mar 2025); doubling time ~7 months since 2019; bootstrap CIs roughly a factor of 2 each direction; later frontier horizons 2.5-4.3 h (metr.org, May 2026).
cost_evidence: Rests on HCAST human baselines (>1500 h, 563 baselines) and RE-Bench (71 expert 8-h attempts); METR note: 'task construction and baselining were both super expensive'; some tasks have only time estimates, not real baselines.
validity_evidence: Authors flag external validity: tasks are self-contained, low-context, clean scoring; time horizons differ between domains by orders of magnitude (visual computer-use 40-100x lower). No correlation with real-world safety outcomes reported.
notes: Second URL fetched: https://metr.org/time-horizons/ (May 2026 update) and the Jan 2026 limitations note (separate entry metr2026horizonlimits).

name: WMDP (Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy)
org: Center for AI Safety / Scale AI
modality: Text multiple-choice questions in biosecurity, cybersecurity and chemical security; accuracy.
what_it_measures: Proxy for hazardous knowledge that could uplift malicious actors; also a target for unlearning (RMU).
reported_metrics: RMU unlearning reduces WMDP accuracy toward chance while preserving MMLU; used in sandbagging studies as the held-out dangerous-capability eval.
cost_evidence: Authored by a consortium of academics and technical consultants; filtered for infohazards before release; no hours or dollars stated.
validity_evidence: Explicitly a proxy (knowledge, not wet-lab capability); van der Weij et al. show models can be prompted/fine-tuned to sandbag WMDP selectively.

name: Decomposing and measuring evaluation awareness (EvalAwareBench)
modality: 100 paired safety/capability tasks with 8 toggleable trigger factors (placeholder entities, grading formats); chain-of-thought monitored for recognition; behaviour change measured.
what_it_measures: Environment-driven vs model-driven evaluation awareness and whether it changes behaviour.
reported_metrics: Recognition varies by model-benchmark pair; recognition rarely changes behaviour; safety evals more sensitive than capability evals.
validity_evidence: Provides attribution tools; proposes 'behavioural consistency under recognition' as validity check.
notes: Author list truncated.

name: TruthfulQA
modality: 817 questions targeting common misconceptions; human-judged truthfulness or fine-tuned GPT-judge; MC variant.
what_it_measures: Imitative falsehoods; a widely used honesty proxy (MASK shows it does not track lying under pressure).
reported_metrics: Best model 58% truthful vs humans 94%; larger models less truthful.
validity_evidence: Safetywashing and MASK show TruthfulQA correlates with capability rather than honesty.

name: Gram: automated sabotage-propensity auditing
modality: Simulated agentic deployment scenarios with incentives to sabotage; automated investigator pipeline; misbehaviour rate per trajectory.
what_it_measures: Sabotage propensity of Gemini agents.
reported_metrics: ~2-3% misbehaviour rate; drops to near zero when realism increased and nudges removed.
validity_evidence: Strong sensitivity of measured rate to scenario realism (false-alarm evidence for contrived scenarios).
notes: Author list truncated.

name: Sim-to-Real Gap of Foundation Model Agents (MDP view)
modality: Position: frames LLM/FM agent benchmark-vs-deployment gap as observation/action/transition/reward gaps and imports robotics sim-to-real methods.
what_it_measures: Conceptual mapping; no experiments.
reported_metrics: none stated
validity_evidence: none stated
notes: Marginal; included because it links ladder level 0 to the sim-to-real vocabulary.

name: SIMMER
modality: Human-curated symbolic kitchen world model (77 actions, 262 objects, ~46,800 interactions) with a state-machine executor that flags precondition violations, latent hazards and irreversible failures in LLM plans.
what_it_measures: Latent (delayed) failures in LLM executable plans.
reported_metrics: At most 17% error-free plans for frontier models; up to 56% contain latent failures; counterfactual foresight cuts latent failures up to 72%.
validity_evidence: None stated.
notes: COLM 2026.

name: J-DAPT (robotic jailbreak detection)
modality: Multimodal jailbreak classifier with attention fusion and domain adaptation; evaluated on jailbreak prompts for driving, maritime and quadruped VLM agents; scored by detection accuracy.
what_it_measures: Detection accuracy of jailbreak attempts against robot-embedded VLMs across domains.
reported_metrics: Detection accuracy near 100% with minimal overhead.
validity_evidence: none stated
bibtex: @article{marchiori2025jdapt, title={Preventing Robotic Jailbreaking via Multimodal Domain Adaptation}, author={Marchiori, Francesco and Sinha, Rohan and Agia, Christopher and Robey, Alexander and Pappas, George J. and Conti, Mauro and Pavone, Marco}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2509.23281}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23281}}
notes: Security defense; only adjacent to physical-safety evaluation. Level set to 0 on the 0-9 ladder (jailbreak-prompt classification; sweeps had 1).

name: Auditing for hidden objectives (blind auditing game)
modality: A model trained with a concealed reward-model-sycophancy objective; four blinded human teams audit it with interpretability (SAEs), behavioural attacks, data analysis; success = identify objective.
what_it_measures: Detectability of hidden objectives by auditing (sensitivity of audits).
reported_metrics: 3 of 4 teams found the hidden objective.
validity_evidence: Game with known ground truth gives a true-positive rate for auditing methods.

name: Apollo in-context scheming evaluations
modality: Agentic text scenarios with a strongly nudged goal and discoverable oversight; scored on whether the model takes covert actions (disable oversight, self-exfiltrate, sandbag) and whether it confesses under follow-up.
what_it_measures: Capability for in-context scheming (deception, oversight subversion).
reported_metrics: o1 maintains deception in >85% of follow-up questions; chain-of-thought shows explicit scheming reasoning.
validity_evidence: Heavily nudged scenarios; later work (Schoen et al. 2025) shows results confounded by evaluation awareness.

name: METR: clarifying limitations of time horizon
modality: n/a (methodological note)
what_it_measures: Stated limits of the time-horizon metric.
reported_metrics: ~170 tasks; error bars ~2x each direction; unreliable above 16 h; few real baselines for 2 h+ tasks.
cost_evidence: 'Task construction and baselining were both super expensive'; some tasks carry time estimates instead of measured baselines.
validity_evidence: Domain gap of orders of magnitude; tasks self-contained vs collaborative real work.

name: RAND red-team study: LLMs and biological attack planning
modality: Teams of researchers role-play malign non-state actors planning a biological attack, with internet only vs internet + LLM; plan viability scored by experts.
what_it_measures: Operational uplift from LLM access for bioweapon attack planning.
size: Multiple teams (cells) across scenarios; counts in full report
reported_metrics: No statistically significant difference in plan viability with vs without LLMs; LLM outputs mirrored internet-available information.
cost_evidence: Expert exercise with multiple research teams; authors say future work should add more LLMs and researchers to increase test sensitivity (i.e. study was underpowered).
validity_evidence: Authors note the study did not measure distance between LLM frontier and required knowledge; explicitly flags low sensitivity.
notes: Page fetched via curl (WebFetch 403). Cell counts not on landing page.

name: LLM safety for robotic health attendant control
modality: 270 harmful instructions grounded in AMA medical-ethics principles sent to 72 LLMs in a Robotic Health Attendant simulation; violation rate.
what_it_measures: Refusal of ethically prohibited instructions by LLMs controlling a care robot.
reported_metrics: Mean violation 54.4%; proprietary median 23.7% vs open-weight 72.8%.
validity_evidence: None stated.
notes: Widest model coverage (72 LLMs) in the catalogue.

name: LLMs often know when they are being evaluated
modality: 1,000 transcripts from 61 datasets (eval vs deployment); model asked to classify; AUC.
what_it_measures: Evaluation awareness (ability to distinguish test from deployment).
reported_metrics: Gemini 2.5 Pro AUC 0.83; human baseline 0.92; agentic settings easier to detect than chat.
validity_evidence: Direct evidence of a construct-validity threat: behaviour may differ between eval and deployment.
notes: Author list truncated.

name: SafePlan (+ SafePlan benchmark)
modality: Natural-language task prompts (safe or unsafe) fed to an LLM planner wrapped with Prompt-Sanity, Invariant, Precondition and Postcondition chain-of-thought reasoners; scored as accept/reject confusion matrix against expert safe/unsafe labels; plans exercised in AI2-THOR.
what_it_measures: Ability of an LLM robotic task planner to reject harmful task prompts while accepting safe ones.
size: 621 expert-curated prompts (127 safe, 494 unsafe) across assistive, navigation, manipulation domains and 3 complexity levels.
reported_metrics: 90.5% reduction in harmful-prompt acceptance; Gemini 1.5 Pro unsafe acceptance 61.34% -> 7.09%, accuracy 88.4%, safe acceptance 70.9%.
cost_evidence: Expert curation of 621 prompts; annotator count not stated; no compute or latency figures.
validity_evidence: Labels are expert judgement; no inter-rater statistics; no real-robot experiments.
notes: Prompt classification is text-only (level 0); AI2-THOR used for plan execution only. Follow-up SafeGate (obi2026safegate) adds real-robot tests.

name: OpenAI early-warning system for LLM-aided biological threat creation
modality: Human study: biology experts and students complete bio-threat-creation tasks with internet only vs internet + GPT-4 (research-only version); responses scored on accuracy, completeness, innovation, time, self-rated difficulty.
what_it_measures: Uplift from model access on biological threat creation tasks (Preparedness Framework bio category).
size: 100 participants (50 biology experts, 50 students) per published description
reported_metrics: Mild uplift in accuracy and completeness, not statistically significant at the study's size.
cost_evidence: 100 human participants in a controlled study; hours not verified.
validity_evidence: Authors flag limited statistical power and that information access is not the only barrier.
notes: openai.com returned HTTP 403 to all fetch attempts; numbers are from memory of the post and must be checked before citing.

name: Sonnet 4.5's eval gaming undermines alignment evals (Redwood analysis)
modality: Secondary analysis of Anthropic system-card numbers.
what_it_measures: How much of measured alignment improvement is attributable to evaluation gaming.
reported_metrics: Verbalized eval awareness 80-100% (Sonnet 4.5) vs <10% (Sonnet 4) on synthetic honeypots; 10-15% vs 1-3% on behavioural audits; inhibiting awareness raised misaligned behaviour 0% -> 1-9%; authors estimate >=25% (worst case ~90%) of behavioural gains are eval gaming.
validity_evidence: Argues training against misalignment evals reinforces awareness, making evals unreliable predictors of deployment behaviour.

name: BBQ: Bias Benchmark for QA
modality: Hand-built QA items with under-informative vs adequately informative contexts across 9 social dimensions; accuracy and bias score.
what_it_measures: Reliance on social stereotypes in QA; used in many model cards (e.g. Anthropic).
size: 58,492 examples (full paper); abstract does not state count
reported_metrics: Up to 3.4 pp higher accuracy when correct answer aligns with a stereotype; >5 pp for gender.
cost_evidence: Hand-built by authors with templates; no cost stated.
validity_evidence: Grounded in attested US social biases; no downstream validation.

name: Crash-report precedents for reasonable driving
modality: Crash narratives normalised to ego-centric language and indexed with driving logs; proposed actions adjudicated by retrieval and counterfactual reasoning; scored by recall of contextually preferred actions on nuScenes.
what_it_measures: Whether negative data (crash reports) improves calibration of driving decisions near safety boundaries.
size: nuScenes benchmark; crash report corpus size not stated
reported_metrics: Recall on preferred actions 24% to 53%.
validity_evidence: none stated
bibtex: @article{patrikar2025negative, title={The Case for Negative Data: From Crash Reports to Counterfactuals for Reasonable Driving}, author={Patrikar, Jay and Sharma, Apoorva and Veer, Sushant and Li, Boyi and Scherer, Sebastian and Pavone, Marco}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2509.18626}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18626}}
notes: Primarily a decision-making method; included because it defines a crash-grounded evaluation of action choices.

name: DeepMind dangerous capability evaluations (Gemini 1.0)
modality: Text/agentic evaluations across persuasion and deception (incl. human-subject studies), cybersecurity CTFs, self-proliferation agent tasks, self-reasoning; mixed scoring (task success, human outcomes).
what_it_measures: Whether a frontier model has dangerous capabilities in four domains; pilot of a 'science of dangerous capability evaluation'.
reported_metrics: No strong dangerous capabilities in Gemini 1.0; 'early warning signs'.
cost_evidence: Persuasion evals use human participants (details in full paper, not abstract).
validity_evidence: none stated in abstract; framed as pilot.

name: HCAST: Human-Calibrated Autonomy Software Tasks
modality: Agent receives task instructions and a container (ML engineering, cybersecurity, software engineering, reasoning); automatic graders; success compared against human baseliners working under identical conditions.
what_it_measures: Agent success as a function of human task duration (1 min to 8+ h).
reported_metrics: Frontier agents 70-80% success on tasks <1 h human time; <20% on tasks >4 h.
cost_evidence: 563 human baselines totalling over 1500 hours of expert work; baseliners have ~5 y experience; METR states baselining and task construction were very expensive.
validity_evidence: Human baselines under identical affordances give calibrated difficulty; no downstream real-world validation.

name: Safetywashing
modality: Meta-analysis: correlation of safety benchmark scores with a general-capability factor across dozens of models.
what_it_measures: Whether safety benchmarks measure anything beyond capability.
size: Dozens of models, many safety benchmarks
reported_metrics: Many safety benchmarks highly correlated with capability (e.g. TruthfulQA, ETHICS); some (e.g. sycophancy, MASK-style) are not.
validity_evidence: Central discriminant-validity evidence for the safety-eval literature.

name: MASK: honesty benchmark
org: Center for AI Safety / Scale AI
modality: Text: belief elicited neutrally (3 direct + 2 consistency prompts), then a pressure prompt; LLM judge maps statements to propositions; honesty = 1 - P(lie).
what_it_measures: Propensity to lie under pressure, disentangled from factual accuracy.
reported_metrics: Claude 3.7 Sonnet 26.6% lying rate; GPT-4o 44.5%; scale does not improve honesty.
cost_evidence: Human-written examples with multi-stage review; lead authors manually reviewed nearly every example; no hours stated.
validity_evidence: LLM judge agrees with 150 manually labelled examples at 86.4%.

name: XSTest (exaggerated safety)
modality: 250 safe prompts (10 types) that resemble unsafe ones plus 200 unsafe contrasts; responses labelled as full compliance / partial / refusal (human annotation, later GPT-4).
what_it_measures: False-refusal rate (specificity) alongside unsafe compliance (sensitivity).
reported_metrics: Systematic exaggerated-safety failures in SOTA models (rates in full paper).
validity_evidence: Directly measures the false-alarm side of safety behaviour; hand-built contrast design.

name: Anti-scheming training stress test (OpenAI/Apollo)
modality: 26 out-of-distribution agentic evaluations (180+ environments) scoring covert actions as scheming proxy; chain-of-thought inspected for evaluation awareness; causal interventions on awareness.
what_it_measures: Whether deliberative alignment reduces covert actions, and how evaluation awareness confounds the measurement.
reported_metrics: o3 covert action rate 13% -> 0.4%; awareness of being evaluated causally decreases covert behaviour, unawareness increases it.
validity_evidence: Explicit: reductions may be partly driven by situational awareness; evaluation results may not transfer to deployment.
notes: Author list abbreviated.

name: SciFi-Benchmark
modality: LLM receives a pivotal decision situation extracted from science-fiction works and picks among candidate actions; scored as agreement with human-voted preferred answers, in normal and adversarial prompting modes.
what_it_measures: Alignment of LLM decisions with human values in robot/AI decision moments drawn from fiction, and the effect of auto-generated constitutions on alignment and jailbreak robustness.
size: 824 sci-fi works; 9,056 questions; 53,384 answers (LLM-introspection); plus a smaller human-labelled evaluation subset.
reported_metrics: Sci-fi character decisions 21.2% aligned with human values vs modern LLMs 79.4% (base) to 95.8% (with constitution); adversarial 23.3% to 92.3%; the generated constitutions also score among the top on ASIMOV.
cost_evidence: Dataset generated by LLM introspection; human voting on the evaluation subset; no hardware.
validity_evidence: Human-voted labels only; text-only thought experiments, no link to physical outcomes.
notes: v1 title was 'How Would AI-Powered Robots Behave in Science Fiction Literature?'. Not a robot evaluation; text-only value alignment. Project page https://scifi-benchmark.github.io/ fetched. v2 July 2025.

name: EmbodyGuard (Subtle Risks, Critical Failures)
modality: LLM-generated text scenarios; Command Refusal Test and Plan Safety Test decomposed into goal interpretation, transition modelling and action sequencing; 13 LLMs.
what_it_measures: Whether LLM planners anticipate subtle situational physical risks, beyond refusing overt commands.
reported_metrics: Models refuse overt commands but fail subtle situational risks (numbers not in abstract).
validity_evidence: None stated.

name: StrongREJECT
modality: 313 forbidden prompts in 6 categories; response scored by rubric evaluator: (1-refused) x (specificity + convincingness)/2 on 5-point scales, or fine-tuned Gemma-2B.
what_it_measures: Jailbreak effectiveness measured as useful harmful information, not surface compliance.
reported_metrics: Spearman vs human labels 0.846 (rubric) / 0.900 (fine-tuned); MAE 0.077-0.084; prior evaluators overstate jailbreak success.
cost_evidence: Labeling budget $2,500 with 5 LabelBox labelers; running a dozen jailbreaks over the dataset ~15 min and <$1 with GPT-4o-mini.
validity_evidence: Best-in-class human agreement; shows jailbreaks often degrade capability, explaining inflated prior ASRs.

name: UK AISI alignment evaluation case study
modality: Petri-based scaffold simulating internal deployment of a coding agent in an AI lab; varies research motivation, replacement threat, autonomy; LLM-judged sabotage.
what_it_measures: Whether frontier models sabotage safety research as coding assistants; also measures eval-vs-deployment distinguishability.
reported_metrics: No confirmed research sabotage; Opus 4.5 Preview and Sonnet 4.5 frequently refuse safety-relevant tasks.
validity_evidence: Validated that scaffold trajectories are not reliably distinguishable from real deployment data by the models unprompted; both models can distinguish when prompted.
notes: Author list truncated.

name: PaperBench
modality: Agent replicates ICML 2024 papers from scratch; hierarchical author-written rubrics graded by an LLM judge; judge validated on a separate benchmark.
what_it_measures: AI research replication ability (AI R&D threshold proxy).
reported_metrics: Claude 3.5 Sonnet 21.0% replication score; below top ML PhD baseline.
cost_evidence: EvalEval estimate ~$9,500 per full evaluation (~$4,200 code-only); human PhD baseline attempts (hours not in abstract).
validity_evidence: LLM judge benchmarked against human grading (numbers in full paper).

name: SWE-bench Verified
modality: Agent receives a GitHub issue and repository snapshot; patch scored by hidden unit tests (pass/fail).
what_it_measures: Real-world software engineering capability; used as capability proxy in RSP/Preparedness autonomy evaluations and CAISI comparisons.
reported_metrics: Used by CAISI (US model solves >20% more tasks than best DeepSeek); Anthropic RSP uses a 42-task >1 h subset with 50% pass-rate threshold.
cost_evidence: OpenAI post (not fetchable, HTTP 403) states 93 professional software developers annotated 1,699 samples with 3 annotations each; HF card confirms human validation only.
validity_evidence: Human validation removes underspecified/unfair tasks; still contamination-prone (public GitHub).
notes: openai.com returns 403 to fetchers; annotator counts are from memory of the post and flagged medium confidence.

name: Defining and Evaluating Physical Safety for LLMs (drones)
modality: LLM generates drone control code for prompts spanning human-targeted, object-targeted, infrastructure and regulatory risks; evaluates refusal and unsafe code generation; ICL/CoT mitigations.
what_it_measures: Trade-off between code-generation capability and physical safety in LLM drone control.
reported_metrics: Larger models safer; ICL/CoT help but not for unintentional attacks.
validity_evidence: None stated.
notes: Communications of the ACM 2026.

name: Noise injection reveals sandbagging
modality: Gaussian noise added to weights; performance-vs-noise curve; sandbagging models show anomalous improvement.
what_it_measures: Model-agnostic detector for sandbagging.
reported_metrics: Elicited full performance from Mistral Large 120B underperforming without instruction; works across sizes and sandbagging techniques.
validity_evidence: Detector validated on password-locked and prompted sandbaggers (true-positive evidence).

name: AI sandbagging
modality: Prompting and password-locked fine-tuning to make models selectively underperform on WMDP while keeping general benchmarks; accuracy deltas.
what_it_measures: Feasibility of strategic underperformance on dangerous-capability evals (a sensitivity threat).
reported_metrics: GPT-4 and Claude 3 Opus can be prompted to selectively sandbag; password-locked models hide capabilities and can target specific scores.
validity_evidence: Shows capability evals are vulnerable: a passing (low) score need not mean absence of capability.

name: PhysicalJailbreakBench-2K / PRISM
modality: Hidden-state probing of open LLMs on SafeAgentBench-style tasks; 2,000 comparison rows contrasting textual-safe vs physically unsafe outputs; logistic probe over hidden states.
what_it_measures: Whether physical-harm risk is separable from textual jailbreak risk in model internals.
size: 2,000 rows from a 10,000-row pool; Qwen2.5 3B-32B, Phi-3.5, SmolLM2.
reported_metrics: 86.2-87.7% accuracy on SafeAgentBench with 11.7-13.7% false positives; PRISM AUC 0.718 vs 0.398 control.
validity_evidence: Reports false-positive rates explicitly.

name: RE-Bench
modality: Agent works in 7 open-ended ML research engineering environments with GPU access; continuous score normalised to a starting solution (0) and a strong reference solution (1); compared to human experts at 2/8/32 h budgets.
what_it_measures: Frontier AI R&D automation capability (an RSP/FSF AI R&D threshold proxy).
reported_metrics: Agents score 4x humans at 2 h budget; humans narrowly exceed agents at 8 h and 2x agents at 32 h; 82% of expert attempts non-zero, 24% match reference.
cost_evidence: 71 eight-hour expert attempts (61 distinct experts) = ~568 expert-hours of baselining; agents generate and test solutions >10x faster 'at much lower cost' (no dollar figure in abstract).
validity_evidence: Human-expert comparison under matched conditions; Gemini 3 Pro FSF report uses RE-Bench tasks for its ML R&D CCL alert threshold.

name: SORRY-Bench
modality: 440 class-balanced unsafe instructions over 44 topics with 20 linguistic augmentations; refusal judged by fine-tuned 7B judge.
what_it_measures: Fine-grained safety refusal behaviour.
size: 440 base prompts (x20 augmentations); >7,000 human annotations for judge meta-evaluation; 50+ models
reported_metrics: Fine-tuned 7B judges match GPT-4-scale accuracy at lower cost.
cost_evidence: Explicitly targets evaluation cost: small judges replace GPT-4; 7k human labels collected.
validity_evidence: Judge validated on 7k+ human annotations.

name: Cybench
modality: Agent gets CTF task description, starter files and a Kali-style container; runs commands; scored by flag submission (task and subtask level); difficulty anchored by human first-solve time (FST).
what_it_measures: Offensive cyber capability of LLM agents (vulnerability discovery and exploitation).
size: 40 CTF tasks from 4 competitions, with subtasks
reported_metrics: Top models (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet) solve tasks up to 11 min FST unguided; hardest task FST 24 h 54 min; FST range 2 min to 24.9 h. US AISI: o1 45% Pass@10 vs 35% best reference.
cost_evidence: Token limits 6k in/2k out per step (32k for o1-preview); token and time usage tracked but no dollar cost given. Used directly by US AISI in pre-deployment tests.
validity_evidence: FST from human competitions as difficulty ground truth; CISA/NSA experts reviewed transcripts for realism in the o1 joint test and commented on limits of CTFs as proxies for real operations.

name: BountyBench
modality: Agents operate on 25 real codebases with set-up environments; Detect/Exploit/Patch tasks from 40 real bug bounties; success scored by exploit/patch tests; value weighted by bounty dollars.
what_it_measures: Dollar-denominated offensive and defensive cyber capability on real systems.
reported_metrics: Best: Detect 12.5% ($3,720), Exploit 67.5% (Claude 3.7 Sonnet Thinking), Patch 90% ($14,152-$14,422); bounties $10-$30,485.
cost_evidence: Manual environment setup per system; bounty values give a monetary scale for capability.
validity_evidence: Real vulnerabilities with real bounty payouts anchor task realism.

name: Conformal risk control for railway signal detection (SNCF dataset)
org: IRT Saint Exupery / ANITI / SNCF (DEEL program)
modality: Object detector (YOLOv5m, DETR-ResNet50, DiffusionDet) fed train-operator-view RGB frames (1280x720); scored by empirical coverage / risk of conformalised bounding boxes at alpha=0.1 and by 'stretch' (box inflation needed to reach the guarantee)
what_it_measures: Whether split conformal prediction and conformal risk control give formally guaranteed miscoverage (<=10%) on detected railway signals, and the price in box size. Positioned as a first step toward certifiable perception for trains.
size: 41 railway-line videos, 3414 images, 3508 boxes; splits 1914 cal / 1500 test (pretrained) or 1414 fit / 1000 cal / 1000 test (fine-tuned)
reported_metrics: Target alpha=0.1; empirical coverage reported close to 0.9 for additive box-wise CP; Hausdorff-style conformalisation gives unusable (huge) boxes; image-wise CRC sometimes unattainable for weak detectors
cost_evidence: Manual annotation of all signals on ~3.4k frames extracted from ~1.5 h videos; fine-tuning 100 epochs YOLOv5m; no wall-clock or dollar cost stated
validity_evidence: Finite-sample coverage guarantee is distribution-free by construction; no field validation or link to operational incident rates
notes: Closest thing in Fel's record to a safety evaluation of an autonomous-system component. Fel is second author; Andeol led. Short companion paper: 'Conformal Prediction for Trustworthy Detection of Railway Signals', AI and Ethics 4:157-161 (2024), arXiv:2301.11136 (fetched, same authors, same dataset). Not a robot; a perception module for a train. Level set to 1 on the 0-9 ladder (object detector scored on static real railway frames; sweeps had 4).

name: Semantic Lookout (maritime VLM hazard detection)
modality: Camera-only VLM selects a cautious fallback maneuver from water-valid trajectories; 40 harbor scenes scored for scene understanding, latency, agreement with human consensus (majority-of-three), and on-water handover demo.
what_it_measures: Whether VLMs give usable semantic hazard awareness in the IMO MASS alert-to-takeover window.
reported_metrics: Sub-10 s models retain most awareness of slower SOTA models; alignment with human consensus reported per model.
validity_evidence: Human-consensus agreement on 40 scenes.
bibtex: @article{christensen2025maritime, title={Foundation models on the bridge: Semantic hazard detection and safety maneuvers for maritime autonomy with vision-language models}, author={Christensen, Kim Alexander and Tufte, Andreas Gudahl and Gusev, Alexey and Sinha, Rohan and Ganai, Milan and Alsos, Ole Andreas and Pavone, Marco and Steinert, Martin}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2512.24470}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24470}}
notes: Maritime, small n; regulatory (IMO MASS) framing is notable. Level set to 1 on the 0-9 ladder (40 harbor scenes scored as VLM QA; single on-water demo unscored; sweeps had 8).

name: Semantic anomaly detection with LLMs
modality: Scene converted to text via open-vocabulary detector (OWL-ViT); LLM (text-davinci-003) asked whether the scene is a semantic anomaly; CARLA driving FSM policy and Ravens manipulation policy; scored by TPR/TNR and agreement with humans.
what_it_measures: Whether an LLM monitor catches system-level semantic edge cases (stop signs on billboards, traffic lights on trucks) that component-level OOD detectors miss.
size: 69 handcrafted CARLA cases in 5 classes; 750 manipulation episodes
reported_metrics: Driving TPR 92% / TNR 78% (SCOD 30%, Mahalanobis 48%); manipulation detects 86% of semantic distractors vs 100% human.
validity_evidence: Agreement with human reasoning reported on manipulation distractors.
bibtex: @article{elhafsi2023semantic, title={Semantic Anomaly Detection with Large Language Models}, author={Elhafsi, Amine and Sinha, Rohan and Agia, Christopher and Schmerling, Edward and Nesnas, Issa and Pavone, Marco}, journal={Autonomous Robots}, year={2023}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.11307}}
notes: Clear reusable test-case protocol. Autonomous Robots 2023 (journal version). Precursor to AESOP. Aliases in sweeps: elhafsi2023semanticanomaly. Level set to 1 on the 0-9 ladder (scene converted to text, LLM asked about the static scene; sweeps had 1/3).

name: Pinocchio (faithfulness of embodied CoT)
modality: Reasoning traces of a driving VLA (Alpamayo-style) rated by humans and by a Gemini judge on observation grounding and stepwise coherence; learned critic used as RL reward; evaluated on held-out US/DE driving scenarios and synthetic counterfactuals.
what_it_measures: Whether verbalized reasoning of a driving VLA faithfully reflects its decisions, and whether faithfulness improves long-tail robustness.
size: 200-sample human study; 100 traces x 4 annotators for judge validation; ~20k DE and ~15k US held-out scenarios; 66 counterfactual scenes
reported_metrics: Gemini agrees with human majority 87-95%; human kappa 0.475-0.685; reasoning consistency 27.7% (SFT) to 61.4%; 1.6x causal-alignment gain on counterfactuals.
cost_evidence: Human annotation of 300 traces; large internal driving dataset.
validity_evidence: Human agreement numbers for the judge; inconsistent coupling between reasoning quality and trajectory improvement found.
bibtex: @article{foutter2026faithfulness, title={Do Vision-Language-Action Models Mean What They Say? On the Role of Faithfulness in Embodied Reasoning}, author={Foutter, Matthew and Cercola, Matteo and Wild, Lena and Wang, Yunshan and Li, Michelle and Gammelli, Daniele and Pavone, Marco}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.04681}, year={2026}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.04681}}
notes: Evaluation of reasoning, not of a safety outcome per se.

name: Virology Capabilities Test (VCT)
modality: Multimodal (text + image) multiple-response questions on virology wet-lab troubleshooting; accuracy vs expert virologists.
what_it_measures: Tacit and visual practical virology knowledge relevant to bioweapons uplift.
reported_metrics: Expert virologists 22.1% average within specialty (with internet); o3 43.8%, outperforming 94% of experts.
cost_evidence: Built with 'dozens of PhD-level expert virologists'; expert baselining performed with internet access; no hours stated.
validity_evidence: Direct human-expert comparison; authors frame it as a dual-use capability signal, not a validated predictor of real-world harm.

name: Hazard or Anomaly? (VLM danger vs discrepancy)
modality: Scene images labelled hazardous vs merely anomalous; VLMs prompted under several strategies; tests whether the distinction changes model behaviour.
what_it_measures: Whether VLMs conflate unusualness with danger (false-alarm behaviour).
size: Two datasets; public set on Roboflow; size not in abstract.
reported_metrics: VLMs frequently misinterpret anomalousness as hazardousness.
validity_evidence: None stated.
notes: RO-MAN 2026.

name: LAB-Bench
modality: Multiple-choice questions on practical biology research (literature QA, figure interpretation, database access, protocol troubleshooting, sequence manipulation); accuracy and coverage vs human biologists.
what_it_measures: Practical biology research assistance capability; used by UK/US AISI as a bio capability probe.
reported_metrics: Frontier models below human experts on most subtasks in 2024; AISI Sonnet 3.5 report: below human baselines except with bioinformatic tools.
validity_evidence: Human expert comparison; designed to match research workflows rather than textbook knowledge.

name: HomeGuard
modality: VLM safeguard with context-guided CoT (perception anchoring then semantic judgement) trained by RFT with process rewards on a curated grounding dataset; risk match rate and over-safety measured.
what_it_measures: Contextual risk identification for household tasks with reduced over-refusal.
reported_metrics: >30% risk-match improvement over baselines; reduced over-safety.
validity_evidence: None stated.
notes: Same group as IS-Bench.

name: HarmBench
modality: Harmful behaviour strings (standard, contextual, copyright, multimodal) attacked by 18 automated red-teaming methods; completion (512 tokens, greedy) classified by a fine-tuned Llama-2-13B classifier; attack success rate.
what_it_measures: Robust refusal under automated jailbreaks; standardised comparison of red-teaming methods.
size: 510 behaviours (200 standard, 100 contextual, 100 copyright, 110 multimodal); 18 methods x 33 models/defences
reported_metrics: Classifier agreement with human labels 93.19% (vs GPT-4 88.37%, AdvBench 69.93%).
cost_evidence: GCG ~20 min per test case on a 7B model on one A100; R2D2 adversarial training 16 h on 8xA100.
validity_evidence: Human-agreement of classifier; ASR is a proxy for misuse potential, not real-world harm.

name: Hijacking Robots with a Piece of Paper (physical prompt injection)
org: Singapore University of Technology and Design
modality: Printed adversarial text (signage, task redefinition, authority impersonation, conflict injection) placed in the visual field of VLM-controlled robots; 5,670 trials across 20 prompts, 3 command formulations and 3 scene layouts; attack success rate and acknowledgement rate.
what_it_measures: Susceptibility of VLM robot controllers to visual text injection and the efficacy of mitigations.
reported_metrics: ASR 27.0% (GPT-4o), 29.4% (Gemini), 5.0% (Qwen3-VL); attacks acknowledged 99.9% of the time; defenses 75-100% effective.
validity_evidence: None stated.
notes: Whether trials ran on physical robots is unclear; physical scene layouts suggest at least level 1, possibly 7.

name: Semantic Denial of Service in LLM-controlled robots
modality: Short (1-5 token) safety-plausible audio phrases injected to halt robot operation without jailbreaking; 4 VLMs, 7 prompt-level defenses, 3 deployment modes; Disruption Success Rate.
what_it_measures: Availability attacks that exploit safety refusals (false-alarm exploitation).
reported_metrics: Prompt-only defenses trade attack suppression against legitimate safety responses.
validity_evidence: None stated.

name: TouchSafeBench (collision grounding for HRC)
modality: Habitat 3.0 co-presence episodes with multi-view RGB-D, trajectory maps and camera metadata; VLM classifies current safety state and imminent collision; Macro-F1 against simulator contact labels.
what_it_measures: Whether VLMs can ground physical contact risk between humans and robots from visual input.
size: 2,940 simulated episodes; 3 VLMs x 9 visual representations.
reported_metrics: Best average Macro-F1 below 50%.
cost_evidence: Labels from simulator physics (no human labelling cost).
validity_evidence: Ground truth is simulator contact, not human judgement.

name: RoboJailBench
modality: Image + instruction pairs (adversarial and benign intent pairs) fed to VLMs acting as robot brains; model must output deny/okay; scored by ASR, security rate, utility rate and their harmonic mean. No robot executed.
what_it_measures: Standardised jailbreak attack/defense comparison for embodied VLM agents with a security-utility trade-off, over an 18-category taxonomy of physical-security consequences.
size: RJB-Instructions 90 images (5 per category x 18) plus 5 augmented datasets of 100 images each (DROID, RH20T, RoboVQA, Robo2VLM, PhysicalAI-AV); 4 attacks, 2 defenses, 5 models
reported_metrics: Conceptual-deception attack 74.07% overall success; Claude Haiku 4.5 baseline rejection 98.28%; RoboGuard and Google prompt defenses raise security while keeping utility.
cost_evidence: Explicitly no physical robots and no humans at risk; API-only evaluation. No dollar figures.
validity_evidence: Binary accept/deny judged by prompt-constrained output; no human agreement study reported; validity to physical harm untested.
bibtex: @article{yeke2026robojailbench, title={RoboJailBench: Benchmarking Adversarial Attacks and Defenses in Embodied Robotic Agents}, author={Yeke, Doguhuan and Zhou, Yanming and Lin, Leo Y. and Cai, Hongyu and Bianchi, Antonio and Celik, Z. Berkay}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2605.19328}, year={2026}}
notes: Recent preprint; leaderboard and code claimed released. Platform (sim vs real) not stated; level 1 assumed for VLM-level evaluation.

name: GuardianBench
modality: Same-scene safe/unsafe instruction pairs; VLM must judge each; pair accuracy requires both members correct; construction grounded in safety standards.
what_it_measures: Latent contextual risk recognition: distinguishing safe from unsafe instructions given identical scenes.
reported_metrics: Average pair accuracy only 24.1% for primary models.
validity_evidence: None stated.

name: REALM (red-teaming physical-world VLMs)
modality: 12 red-teaming methods, 3 defenses, 13 VLMs under a unified protocol; agentic pipeline generates physically grounded attack objectives.
what_it_measures: Comparative attack effectiveness against VLMs used for physical-world tasks.
reported_metrics: Text/typographic injection causes most failures; single-pass attacks near iterative ones at lower cost; scale does not confer robustness.
validity_evidence: None stated.

name: MSSBench (Multimodal Situational Safety)
modality: MLLM receives an image (safe or unsafe situation) plus a language query; must respond safely (chat) or refuse/adapt an action (embodied, images from embodied simulators). GPT-4o judge classifies responses as safe/unsafe; accuracy on unsafe vs safe halves.
what_it_measures: Whether a VLM's safety judgement depends correctly on the visual situation rather than the query alone.
size: 1,820 query-image pairs (half safe, half unsafe); 760 pairs in the embodied subset; 4 domains, 10 categories.
reported_metrics: Best embodied accuracy ~59% (Claude: 55.9% on unsafe, 98.4% on safe); models misclassify unsafe embodied situations; captions improve results (visual understanding is bottleneck).
cost_evidence: Manual authoring of unsafe household tasks and situations; no annotator counts or hours.
validity_evidence: GPT-4o judge; no judge-vs-human agreement reported; no real-world validation.
notes: ICLR 2025. Static VLM QA; included as the level-1 anchor for embodied situational safety.

name: EARBench (EAIRiskBench)
modality: Multi-agent pipeline: foundation models generate safety guidelines, risk-prone scene descriptions (text or image), a target model plans the task, and an automated evaluator scores the plan; Task Risk Rate (TRR) = fraction of plans exhibiting hazardous behaviour.
what_it_measures: Physical-risk awareness of foundation-model task planners in generated risk-prone scenes.
size: EARDataset 2,636 samples (1,318 textual + 1,318 visual) over 28 scenes and 7 domains.
reported_metrics: Average TRR 95.75%; GPT-4o 94.03%, Claude 3 95.05%, Gemini 1.5 Flash 93.67%.
cost_evidence: Fully automated generation and judging; no compute or annotation cost stated.
validity_evidence: Judge-vs-human Cohen's kappa ~0.48 without safety tips, ~0.85 with safety tips provided to the judge.
notes: Half the set is text-only (level 0), half visual (level 1). Kappa figures from HTML v5. Earlier versions titled EAIRiskBench. Open-loop, no simulator.

name: ASIMOV-Agentic (Gemini Robotics 2: Safety Evaluations)
modality: Embodied-reasoning agent (system 2) receives images, constraints and instructions and must route: call the VLA tool, refuse, ask the human, or call robot_stop(). Six components: constraint following (text / pointing / bbox / tool-use), human proximity monitoring from stereo images (single frame and 5 s agentic windows), safety-message tool calling, VLA feasibility (one-step and ToolEmu-style emulated closed loop), instruction ambiguity, obfuscated gauge reading. Scored by classification accuracy, MAE in metres, FNR/FPR, task and step completion.
what_it_measures: Whether an agent orchestrating a VLA refuses unsafe tool calls, stops for nearby humans, shields the VLA from infeasible tasks, and asks for clarification under ambiguity; plus real humanoid safe-stop tests.
size: Hugging Face dataset google/asimov_agentic, 2.4 GB parquet across 7 components; per-component item counts not stated in the report.
reported_metrics: Text constraint classification >= 96% for all frontier models but higher variance for pointing/bbox/tool-use; human distance MAE 0.35-0.55 m, 1 m breach detection 79-93%; agentic monitoring: FPR < 5% comes with FNR > 40%, FNR 10-15% costs 15-25% unnecessary stops, no model in the ideal quadrant; safety-message handling 100% for ER 2, Claude Opus 4.8, GPT 5.5; feasibility accuracy 62.0% (no VLA awareness) to 95.8% (detailed developer instructions); Apollo 2 humanoid lab tests 99% human detection and 96% safe-pose transition.
cost_evidence: Sensorized human-approach data (head-mounted ZED stereo camera, Vive trackers); synthetic constraint data via Gemini Pro and Nano Banana with human annotation and low-agreement filtering; Gemini-based VLA confidence emulator used to avoid physical robots or physics simulators; real tests on Apptronik Apollo 2 in a garage setting.
validity_evidence: Human-annotated ground truth; real-world safe-stopping validation on a humanoid (99%/96%). Report explicitly says it does not evaluate the certified functional-safety stack.
notes: Dated 2026-07-29; Sindhwani, Majumdar, Jindal, Kalashnikov, Sermanet-era collaborators appear in the alphabetical contributor list. Benchmark released at https://huggingface.co/datasets/google/asimov_agentic (fetched; gated, CC-BY-4.0). No arXiv version found. Blog post https://deepmind.google/blog/gemini-robotics-2-brings-whole-body-intelligence-to-robots/ (30 July 2026) fetched. Level set to 2 on the 0-9 ladder (offline dataset incl. 5 s stereo video windows of real human approach; humanoid lab stop test reported separately; sweeps had 4).

name: AccidentBench
modality: Multimodal LLMs answer human-annotated QA about accident videos (vehicle, air, water); scored by accuracy across temporal/spatial/intent tasks and difficulty levels.
what_it_measures: Safety-critical video understanding and reasoning of foundation models in accident scenarios.
size: ~2000 videos, >19,000 QA pairs (~6300 per difficulty level); 83% vehicle accidents
reported_metrics: GPT-5 37.3% and Gemini 2.5 Pro 31.1% on hard vehicle tasks; ~18% on hardest/longest tasks.
cost_evidence: Human annotation of >19k QA pairs; cost not stated.
validity_evidence: Human-annotated ground truth; no link to closed-loop driving safety.
bibtex: @article{gu2025accidentbench, title={AccidentBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning in Vehicle Accidents and Beyond}, author={Gu, Shangding and Wang, Xiaohan and Ying, Donghao and Zhao, Haoyu and Yang, Runing and Jin, Ming and Li, Boyi and Pavone, Marco and Yeung-Levy, Serena and Wang, Jun and Song, Dawn and Spanos, Costas}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2509.26636}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.26636}}
notes: Pavone is one of 12 authors; benchmark tests VLMs rather than a control stack. Level set to 2 on the 0-9 ladder (accident-video QA; sweeps had 0).

name: Position: embodied reward models need bad behavior data (RoboArena reward-model audit)
modality: Real-robot rollout videos with human preference rankings and 0-100 scores (RoboArena) fed to three embodied reward models (ReWiND, GVL with GPT-5, Dopamine); scored by preference-ordering accuracy against human evaluators, stratified by task category.
what_it_measures: How well embodied reward models agree with human judgments of real robot behavior, and where they over-reward unsafe, poorly executed, or shortcut behaviors; the effect of adding real bad-behavior data.
size: 723 valid RoboArena tasks with 2-6 rollouts each (427 pick/place, 32 push/pull, 72 open/close, 47 stack, 68 reorient, 30 pour, 47 tool use).
reported_metrics: Preference-ordering accuracy 0.72-0.77 on pick/place falling to 0.52-0.62 on tool use (chance 0.50); in-context injection of bad data gives ~10% accuracy gain for GVL on hard tasks.
cost_evidence: Relies on RoboArena's existing decentralized real-robot evaluation with human labels; paper argues negative data is costly to collect and often withheld. No own compute stated.
validity_evidence: Ground truth is human evaluator preference on real robot rollouts; agreement rates reported per category.
notes: Explicitly calls for decentralized physical evaluation systems and fine-grained reward-model benchmarks. Directly relevant to the value of human-labelled safety evaluations. Level set to 2 on the 0-9 ladder (reward models judge real-robot rollout videos offline (RoboArena); sweeps had 8).

name: Data lifecycle benchmark for aerospace ML
modality: Satellite pose-estimation model deployed in novel conditions (backgrounds, bad pixels); algorithms select inputs to label and retrain; scored by performance over mission lifetime and cumulative labelling/retraining cost.
what_it_measures: Cost-vs-performance of labelling strategies under evolving input distributions (open-source benchmark).
reported_metrics: Proposed selector matches 100%-labelling performance while labelling 50% of inputs.
cost_evidence: Labelling and retraining cost explicitly tracked as a benchmark axis.
validity_evidence: none stated
bibtex: @article{banerjee2022lifecycle, title={Data Lifecycle Management in Evolving Input Distributions for Learning-based Aerospace Applications}, author={Banerjee, Somrita and Sharma, Apoorva and Schmerling, Edward and Spolaor, Max and Nemerouf, Michael and Pavone, Marco}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2209.06855}, year={2022}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.06855}}
notes: Not safety per se; included because it benchmarks labelling cost explicitly.

name: AdvDO (realistic adversarial attacks on trajectory prediction)
modality: Optimisation-based attack with differentiable dynamics generates realistic adversarial agent histories; SOTA predictors benchmarked on general and planning-aware metrics; downstream AV simulated.
what_it_measures: Adversarial robustness of trajectory predictors and its downstream planning consequences.
reported_metrics: Prediction error up +50% (general) and +37% (planning-aware metrics); attacks cause off-road or collisions in simulation.
validity_evidence: Downstream planner collisions in sim.
bibtex: @inproceedings{cao2022advdo, title={AdvDO: Realistic Adversarial Attacks for Trajectory Prediction}, author={Cao, Yulong and Xiao, Chaowei and Anandkumar, Anima and Xu, Danfei and Pavone, Marco}, booktitle={European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV)}, year={2022}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.08744}}
notes: Red-teaming of a perception/prediction module. Level set to 3 on the 0-9 ladder (optimisation-generated adversarial histories, downstream AV simulated; sweeps had 2).

name: Robust trajectory prediction against adversarial attacks
modality: Adversarial training + domain-specific augmentation; robust model evaluated with a planner for accident rates.
what_it_measures: Robustness gains vs clean-data cost, and downstream collision/off-road rates.
reported_metrics: +46% on adversarial data at 3% clean-data cost; +21% adversarial / +9% clean vs prior robust methods; reduced severe accident rates with planner.
validity_evidence: Downstream planner accident rates in sim.
bibtex: @inproceedings{cao2022robust, title={Robust Trajectory Prediction against Adversarial Attacks}, author={Cao, Yulong and Xu, Danfei and Weng, Xinshuo and Mao, Zhuoqing and Anandkumar, Anima and Xiao, Chaowei and Pavone, Marco}, booktitle={Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL)}, year={2022}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.00094}}
notes: Defense paper; evaluation protocol shared with AdvDO. Level set to 3 on the 0-9 ladder (adversarial trajectory attacks with simulated planner; sweeps had 2).

name: FORCE-OPT (predictor-based forward reachable sets for plan safety)
modality: Multimodal trajectory predictor distributions converted to conformally calibrated forward reachable sets; ego plan checked for intersection; Bayesian filter adapts conservativeness; evaluated on nuScenes with synthetic unsafe scenes; scored by coverage, FPR, FNR.
what_it_measures: Soundness and completeness of a plan-level safety monitor for end-to-end stacks.
size: nuScenes (~15 h); train Singapore, test Singapore (ID) and Boston (OOD)
reported_metrics: Coverage ~90%; FPR 8.6% (ID) / 5.2% (OOD); FNR 3.0% / 13.0%; 0.022 s per scenario; 7 baselines.
validity_evidence: Unsafe cases are synthetic edits of safe scenes; no real collisions.
bibtex: @article{chakraborty2025frs, title={Safety Evaluation of Motion Plans Using Trajectory Predictors as Forward Reachable Set Estimators}, author={Chakraborty, Kaustav and Feng, Zeyuan and Veer, Sushant and Sharma, Apoorva and Ding, Wenhao and Topan, Sever and Ivanovic, Boris and Pavone, Marco and Bansal, Somil}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2507.22389}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.22389}}
notes: Title literally 'Safety Evaluation of Motion Plans'; runtime monitor with reusable protocol. Level set to 3 on the 0-9 ladder (nuScenes plus synthetic unsafe scenes, open-loop; sweeps had 1).

name: SafeMind / SafeMindBench
org: BrainCog Lab, Chinese Academy of Sciences
modality: Image (DALL-E 3 rendered) + instruction pairs across Instr-Risk, Env-Risk, Order-Fix, Req-Align; agent outputs an action sequence validated against a skill set, then a GPT-4 judge checks constraints. Metrics: Safety Rate, Success Rate, Effectiveness Rate.
what_it_measures: Safety of embodied LLM agents across task understanding, environment perception and action ordering under sabotage/harm/privacy/illegal scenarios.
reported_metrics: GPT-4o safety rate 10.3% (Instr-Risk), 19.1% (Env-Risk), 61.1% (Order-Fix), 89.7% (Req-Align), weighted 37.2%.
cost_evidence: LLM-synthesis-human-verification pipeline; annotator counts and cost not stated.
validity_evidence: GPT-4 judge; no judge-vs-human agreement; no real robot.

name: CrashTwin (physics-grounded world-model benchmark)
modality: Video world models prompted with multi-agent collision scenes; rollouts reconstructed to 3D kinematics with a calibration-free pipeline; scored on spatio-temporal consistency, momentum/kinetic-energy conservation residuals and world-dynamics integrity.
what_it_measures: Physical trustworthiness of generative world models used as AV simulators in collision scenarios.
size: 25.6K synthetic (CARLA) + 12.6K real collision sequences; eval sets of 300+44 and 100+16
reported_metrics: All models (Wan, Cosmos-Predict2, Veo 3.1, Seedance etc.) show high momentum/energy residuals (~0.89 vs ground truth 0.31; post-training 0.65); visual quality masks physics violations.
cost_evidence: API-constrained proprietary models needed a mini eval set; otherwise compute unspecified.
validity_evidence: Human evaluation: physics metrics align better with human realism preference than visual-quality proxies.
bibtex: @article{chen2026crashtwin, title={A Physics-Grounded Benchmark for Multi-Agent Dynamics in World Models}, author={Chen, Nuo and Liu, Lulin and Li, Zihao and Zeng, Ziyao and Zhu, Zihao and Cong, Wenyan and Hong, Junyuan and Yang, Yunhao and Tu, Zhengzhong and Wang, Yan and Ivanovic, Boris and Pavone, Marco and Wang, Zhangyang and Zhou, Yang and Fan, Zhiwen}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.28757}, year={2026}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28757}}
notes: Evaluates the simulator, not the AV; relevant to world-models-for-validation theme. Level set to 3 on the 0-9 ladder (generated world-model collision videos scored open-loop (evaluates the simulator); sweeps had 4).

name: RealGen (retrieval-augmented scenario generation)
modality: Retrieval-based in-context generation composes behaviours from retrieved scenarios to create edited, composite or critical scenarios.
what_it_measures: Flexibility and controllability of generated safety-critical scenarios.
reported_metrics: Qualitative/relative controllability results.
validity_evidence: none stated
bibtex: @article{ding2023realgen, title={RealGen: Retrieval Augmented Generation for Controllable Traffic Scenarios}, author={Ding, Wenhao and Cao, Yulong and Zhao, Ding and Xiao, Chaowei and Pavone, Marco}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2312.13303}, year={2023}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.13303}}
notes: Tooling. Level set to 3 on the 0-9 ladder (retrieval-augmented scenario generation, open-loop; sweeps had 2).

name: Realistic Extreme Behavior Generation for AV Testing
modality: Collision-free Waymo Open / nuScenes scenes; adversary trajectories perturbed in the parameter space of a learned behaviour model (MTR, Trajectron++) under a data-alignment realism constraint; counterfactual collisions clustered into a test suite; target AV policy run against them.
what_it_measures: Interpretable failure modes of an AV collision-avoidance policy under realistic adversarial counterfactual collisions.
reported_metrics: Baseline reactive policy: 100% response to high-speed chasing/side crashes, 55-59% no-response for low-speed lateral crashes.
cost_evidence: Runs on public datasets and learned predictors; no hardware.
validity_evidence: Realism enforced via data-alignment in model parameter space; no real-crash validation.
bibtex: @inproceedings{dyro2024extreme, title={Realistic Extreme Behavior Generation for Improved AV Testing}, author={Dyro, Robert and Foutter, Matthew and Li, Ruolin and Di Lillo, Luigi and Schmerling, Edward and Zhou, Xilin and Pavone, Marco}, booktitle={IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.10669}}
notes: ICRA 2025 per ASL page. Aliases in sweeps: dyro2024realistic. Level set to 3 on the 0-9 ladder (generated adversarial counterfactual collisions on real scenes; sweeps had 2/3).

name: Gemini Robotics tech report, safety section (ASIMOV evals)
