modality: Gemini Robotics-ER evaluated on ASIMOV-Multimodal (image + action VQA) and ASIMOV-Injury (text) semantic-safety sets and on content-safety pointing queries; scored by alignment/rejection rates.
what_it_measures: Semantic action safety of the ER model before and after post-training on ASIMOV data, and refusal of bias-inducing pointing queries.
size: Not stated in the report (uses ASIMOV datasets, see sermanet2025asimov).
reported_metrics: 96% rejection of bias-inducing pointing queries vs 20% baseline; qualitative improvement in semantic safety after ASIMOV post-training.
validity_evidence: Report explicitly scopes to semantic safety; no collision/force testing numbers for Gemini Robotics-ER.
notes: Sindhwani confirmed in author list. Safety is Section 5 of a capability report; evaluation content is secondary. Cite only for the 96% vs 20% figure and the layered safety approach. 118+ authors; key reused from speaker-sindhwani.json.

name: Gemini Robotics 1.5 tech report: ASIMOV-2.0 + Auto-Red-Teaming (ART)
modality: Attacker / Target / AutoRater LLM triad: attacker generates prompt attacks, scene attacks (edited images) and environment attacks (moving obstacles during rollouts) against Gemini Robotics; AutoRater judges failures such as hallucinated pointing. Also reports ASIMOV-2.0 safety evaluation of GR-ER 1.5.
what_it_measures: Adversarial robustness of the robot foundation model to prompt, scene and environment attacks, and semantic safety on ASIMOV-2.0 (risk recognition, consequence understanding, intervention triggering, safety-constrained pointing).
size: Not stated (number of attacks not reported).
reported_metrics: Qualitative: GR-ER 1.5 improves over GR-ER on ASIMOV-2.0 and reaches state of the art on safety-constrained pointing with 'thinking about safety' fine-tuning; no attack success rates published. Orchestrator failure analysis: planning failures 25.5% to 9%.
validity_evidence: AutoRater said to 'reliably detect' hallucinations; no human validation of the AutoRater reported.
notes: Sindhwani confirmed in author list. ART is the group's only red-teaming protocol description; numbers are withheld, so cite for the protocol shape, not for evidence. Level set to 3 on the 0-9 ladder (attacker/target/autorater protocol on prompts and edited scenes; numbers withheld; sweeps had 4).

name: VLESA
modality: Egocentric frames with goal-conditioned safety annotations; GRPO-trained safety Q-filter plus intent-action predictor; evaluated on ASIMOV-2.0 intervention-frame accuracy.
what_it_measures: Real-time intervention triggering from egocentric video of human activity.
reported_metrics: Q-filter improves action safety >41 points; higher exact-frame intervention accuracy than baselines.
validity_evidence: Evaluated on ASIMOV-2.0 human-consensus labels.

name: ASIMOV-2.0 (Can AI Perceive Physical Danger and Intervene?)
modality: Foundation model receives text injury scenarios (ASIMOV-2.0-Injury), photorealistic generated videos of safe-to-unsafe transitions (ASIMOV-2.0-Video), or image + embodiment constraint text (ASIMOV-2.0-Constraints). Scored by accuracy on risk type, severity, intervention timing, and constraint-violation rate against consensus human labels.
what_it_measures: Whether frontier models can perceive latent physical danger, judge injury severity, decide when to intervene, and respect embodiment-specific constraints (payload, gripper geometry) supplied via system instructions; also evaluates a 'thinking about safety' post-training recipe.
size: 319 text injury scenarios; 287 generated videos; 164 image-constraint pairs (validation sets).
reported_metrics: Top models (GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Opus 4.1) 92.3% average accuracy on risk-type recognition but 87.7-88.7% on severity; video-vs-text accuracy gaps of 27% (Claude Opus 4.1) and 40% (GPT-5); constraint violation rates 38.6-75% across models; fine-tuned Gemini Robotics-ER achieves the lowest violation rate with 50% shorter reasoning traces.
cost_evidence: Generator-critic-refine pipeline using Gemini 2.5 Pro, Imagen and Veo 3; 5 human raters per instance; video items kept only if rater timestamp std dev < 1.0 s; constraint items require >= 80% rater consensus; no robot hardware.
validity_evidence: Ground truth is filtered human consensus; scenarios grounded in real NEISS hospital injury reports (~100 hospitals, ~500K injuries/year). No correlation with deployed-robot incident rates reported.
notes: Sindhwani last author. Speaker homepage lists it under CoRL 2026; an OpenReview entry (go44bcifFA) exists but could not be fetched, so venue not independently confirmed. Project page https://asimov-benchmark.github.io/v2/ fetched. Injury track is level 0; constraints and video tracks are generated media (level 3). Project page asimov-benchmark.github.io/v2 fetched: data via Colab, no leaderboard numbers on page.

name: ICAT (incident-case-grounded adaptive testing of world models)
modality: Structured risk memories built from real incident reports and safety manuals are retrieved to compose risk cases with causal chains and severity labels; video world models are tested on whether generated futures show the hazard mechanism and severity.
what_it_measures: Physical-risk fidelity of generative world models used as neural simulators.
reported_metrics: Mainstream world models miss mechanisms/triggers and miscalibrate severity.
validity_evidence: Grounded in real incident reports; no quantitative human agreement.
notes: Relevant to validity of level-3/5 generative evaluations.

name: Predictive Red Teaming (RoboART)
modality: Visuomotor diffusion policy; its RGB observations are edited with Imagen 3 along language-specified environmental factors, a policy-specific embedding anomaly detector predicts success rate as 1 - anomaly rate; predictions are compared with real hardware success rates.
what_it_measures: Which off-nominal environmental conditions (lighting, background, distractors, table height) break an imitation-learned policy, predicted without running the robot, and how well those predictions match real deployment.
size: 12 off-nominal conditions; 2 diffusion policies of different architecture; 500+ hardware trials (20+ per factor).
reported_metrics: Average absolute gap between predicted and real success rate < 0.19 (0.1 on the project page); Spearman rank correlation 0.8 between predicted and real factor rankings; targeted data collection improves performance 2-7x in predicted-bad conditions and 2-5x in unseen conditions.
cost_evidence: 500+ real hardware trials for ground truth; generative image editing replaces hardware trials for prediction; compute not quantified.
validity_evidence: Direct validation: predicted vs real success rates on hardware (Spearman 0.8, mean gap < 0.19).
notes: CoRL 2025 per speaker homepage. Best sim-vs-real validation evidence among the speaker's evals. Project page https://predictive-red-team.github.io/ fetched. Level 3 for the predictor; validation ladder level 7. Not adversarial in the security sense; it is distribution-shift red teaming. safety_focus false: targets task-success robustness, not hazard behaviour, but is the cleanest proxy-validity study. Sweeps disagreed on safety_focus; kept True from the richest record. Level set to 3 on the 0-9 ladder (Imagen-edited observations scored open-loop; validated against 500+ hardware trials; sweeps had 3/6).

name: EgoSafetyBench
modality: Synthetic egocentric robot-view videos (Kling v3 text-to-video) annotated at 0.5 s granularity; VLM acts as streaming guard and must flag hazards; contrastive ladders differ by a single deciding cue. Metrics: chunk-level hazard recall, false-alarm rate on safe content, timely detection within 0.5 s.
what_it_measures: Runtime hazard detection and over-intervention of VLMs on temporally evolving egocentric scenes.
reported_metrics: Claude-Sonnet-4.6: ~79% chunk-level hazard recall, 17.3% false alarms on safe content, 57.4% timely detection; Gemini-3.5-Flash false alarms rise 16.0% -> 36.6% with misleading signs; weak models miss up to a third of hazards.
cost_evidence: Two annotators per video plus third resolver; no hours/dollars; videos generated not filmed.
validity_evidence: Inter-annotator agreement 91.2% (kappa 0.744) chunk-level, 90.5% (kappa 0.804) video-level. No real-footage or outcome validation.
notes: Best-documented inter-annotator agreement in the catalogue; reports both sensitivity and false-alarm behaviour.

name: LD-Scene
modality: Latent diffusion trajectory model guided by LLM-written adversarial loss functions (CoT code generator + debugger) from natural-language user queries; nuScenes; scored by realism, diversity, adversarial effectiveness.
what_it_measures: User-controllable generation of adversarial driving scenarios without expert knowledge.
reported_metrics: State-of-the-art on realism/diversity/effectiveness (numbers not in abstract).
validity_evidence: none stated
bibtex: @article{peng2025ldscene, title={LD-Scene: LLM-Guided Diffusion for Controllable Generation of Adversarial Safety-Critical Driving Scenarios}, author={Peng, Mingxing and Xie, Yuting and Guo, Xusen and Yao, Ruoyu and Yang, Hai and Ma, Jun}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2505.11247}, year={2025}}
notes: Open-loop trajectory generation on nuScenes; closed-loop use unclear.

name: HomeSafe-Bench (unsafe action detection)
modality: Videos built from physical simulation plus video generation depicting embodied-agent actions; VLM must detect unsafe behaviour and temporally localise the hazard; HD-Guard hierarchical monitor proposed.
what_it_measures: Detection and temporal localisation of embodied-agent-specific unsafe actions in household video.
reported_metrics: Bottlenecks in VLM-based safety detection identified; HD-Guard gives better latency-performance trade-off (numbers not in abstract).
validity_evidence: None stated.

name: Vision-foundation-model embedding semantic anomaly detection
modality: Runtime images embedded with a vision foundation model (grid or instance-based) and compared to a nominal-scenario database; CARLA-simulated anomalies; compared with GPT-4o.
what_it_measures: Detection and localisation of semantic anomalies for driving.
reported_metrics: Instance-based method with filtering comparable to GPT-4o, with localisation.
validity_evidence: none stated
bibtex: @inproceedings{ronecker2025vfm, title={Vision Foundation Model Embedding-Based Semantic Anomaly Detection}, author={Ronecker, Max Peter and Foutter, Matthew and Elhafsi, Amine and Gammelli, Daniele and Barakaiev, Ihor and Pavone, Marco and Watzenig, Daniel}, booktitle={ICRA 2025 Workshop on Safe VLMs}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.07998}}
notes: Workshop paper.

name: StressDream (steered world-model policy evaluation)
modality: Policy actions + current observation fed to a diffusion video world model (Vista for driving, Ctrl-World for manipulation); initial noise is optimized with a VLM semantic objective plus a plausibility objective to steer imagined futures toward text-specified high-impact events (e.g. task failure, collision); policies scored by whether plausible steered futures contain the undesirable outcome.
what_it_measures: Whether a policy's actions admit plausible failure futures under a video world model, used for robust offline policy evaluation and for weighting fine-tuning data. Measures recall of failure events found per imagination budget and downstream policy success after robust fine-tuning.
size: Driving: 100 image-action-text pairs across 8 safety-critical event categories plus 200 imminent-collision examples. Manipulation: 6 contact-rich tasks, ~150 teleop trajectories per task, 100 failure trajectories for evaluation, 40 successful demos per task for fine-tuning. Plus a Dubins-car controlled study.
reported_metrics: Failure-event recall 54% to 94% vs nominal sampling (manipulation); pi0.5 VLA success 39% to 71% after robust fine-tuning; Dubins car: high TPR while keeping high TNR (steers to failure only when plausible).
cost_evidence: 20 noise-optimization steps (driving) and 10 (manipulation) per imagination; authors note current WMs take several minutes per imagination; Vista noise dim ~922K, Ctrl-World ~58K. No GPU-hour total stated.
validity_evidence: Dubins-car ground truth shows steering finds failures only when dynamically plausible; manipulation failures judged by human labelling of generated videos; driving quality checked with WorldModelBench. Authors state plausibility is limited to what the WM supports and does not imply physical plausibility; no real-robot rollouts confirm predicted failures.
notes: Most directly eval-centric Bajcsy paper. Co-authored with Marco Pavone (also a SPAIS speaker link). Code: https://github.com/CMU-IntentLab/StressDream, project page https://junwon.me/StressDream/ (both fetched, 200). Venue CoRL 2026 per lab publications page. Co-authored with Andrea Bajcsy (also a workshop-relevant speaker). World-model-based evaluation. Level set to 3 on the 0-9 ladder (steered world-model imaginations scored open-loop; no real-robot closed loop; sweeps had 2/3).

name: ASIMOV Benchmark v1 + generated robot constitutions
modality: VLM/LLM receives (a) an Imagen-3-edited hazardous version of a real ego-centric home/office frame plus a candidate instruction (ASIMOV-Multimodal), (b) a text injury scenario from hospital reports plus an action (ASIMOV-Injury), (c) an ethical dilemma (ASIMOV-Dilemmas). Scored as binary desirable/undesirable classification accuracy against human-voted labels ('alignment rate'), in normal and adversarial prompting modes.
what_it_measures: Whether a VLM judges robot actions as safe/unsafe the way humans do (semantic safety), and how much auto-generated constitutions raise that alignment versus no-constitution and human-written constitutions.
size: 513,679 contexts / 2,942,060 instructions total (train); validation: Multimodal-Auto 50 contexts/1,311 instr (789 human-labelled), Multimodal-Manual 59/159, Injury 50/319 (163 human-labelled), Dilemmas-Auto 100/200 (35 human-labelled), Dilemmas-SciFi 51/284 (153 human-labelled).
reported_metrics: Top alignment 84.3% (Robot-Constitution128-AutoMerge-AutoAmend10, averaged over normal+adversarial), beating no-constitution and human-written constitutions.
cost_evidence: Generation is automatic (VLM proposes edits, Imagen 3 renders); only ~1,140 validation instructions are human-labelled. No hours, dollars or rater counts stated.
validity_evidence: Ground truth is human voting on desirability; no inter-rater kappa reported; no real-robot or outcome validation. Authors state constitutions are 'for research purposes only, not for deployments requiring safety guarantees'.
notes: Injury subset is text-only (level 0); multimodal subsets are synthetic edited scenes (level 3). CoRL 2025 (PMLR v305). Sizes from Table 1 of the HTML full text. Sindhwani is last author. CoRL 2025 per project page and speaker homepage. Project page https://asimov-benchmark.github.io/v1/ also fetched. Low-ladder contrast case (level 3); included to anchor the cost/validity trade-off against level-7/9 entries. Level set to 3 on the 0-9 ladder (generated images plus text QA, scored against human votes; sweeps had 1/2/3).

name: LCTGen (language-conditioned traffic generation)
modality: LLM + transformer decoder selects map location and initial traffic and dynamics from text.
what_it_measures: Realism/fidelity of generated traffic scenes conditioned on language.

validity_evidence: Negative evidence from others: PolaRiS finds LIBERO scores cluster at 90-95% regardless of real performance; LIBERO-PRO shows 90%+ collapsing to 0% under object/instruction perturbation; LIBERO-Plus 95% to <30% under camera/initial-state shifts; vla-eval shows single undocumented parameters move scores by up to 55 pp.
notes: Saturated; useful mainly as the cautionary example.

name: JailWAM
modality: Adversarial instructions against world action models (LingBot-VA) in RoboTwin; dual-path verification (risk screening + simulation) with a three-level risk discriminator.
what_it_measures: Jailbreak success against world-action robot models.
reported_metrics: 84.2% attack success on LingBot-VA.
validity_evidence: None stated.

name: IS-Bench
modality: VLM-driven agent acts in OmniGibson household scenes from egocentric observations; process-oriented evaluation checks that risk-mitigation actions occur before/after specific risk-prone steps. Metrics: Success Rate, Safe Success Rate, Safety Recall, Safety Awareness.
what_it_measures: Interactive safety: whether an embodied VLM agent perceives emergent risks during execution and orders mitigation steps correctly, not just post-hoc plan safety.
size: 161 scenarios, 388 unique safety risks, 10 domestic safety categories; risks 24.2% pre-caution / 75.8% post-caution.
reported_metrics: GPT-4o SR 81.3% but SSR 33.8%; safety-aware CoT +9.3% safety but -9.4% task success.
cost_evidence: One A100 80GB; each evaluation session 2.5-3 h depending on VLM inference time. Every reference plan manually executed and verified by human annotators in the simulator.
validity_evidence: Ground truth is human-verified executable plans; no inter-annotator statistics; no real-world transfer evidence.
notes: AAAI 2026. Rare explicit wall-clock cost statement. AAAI 2026. OmniGibson is photoreal-ish, so level 5. Level set to 4 on the 0-9 ladder (OmniGibson physics simulation; sweeps had 4/5).

name: Sample-efficient safety assurances via conformal prediction
modality: Warning system + simulator of robot/environment dynamics; conformal prediction tunes alert threshold to a provable false-negative rate; applied to a driver warning system and robotic grasping.
what_it_measures: Guaranteed false-negative rate of unsafe-situation warning systems using as few as 1/epsilon calibration samples.
reported_metrics: Empirically achieves guaranteed FNR with low FPR in both applications.
validity_evidence: Provable FNR under exchangeability; empirical confirmation.

name: SafeStage

name: ForesightSafety-VLA
org: BrainCog Lab, Chinese Academy of Sciences (Yi Zeng)

reported_metrics: CC 0.18 (OpenVLA-OFT) to 0.39 (ACT); unsafe share of successful episodes 12.5% (OpenVLA-OFT), 25.0% (RDT), 29.4% (DP), 37.5% (ACT). Structure and visual variation degrade safety more than language variation.
cost_evidence: Language templates W0-W2 human-authored, W3-W4 LLM-generated then manually verified; no compute or wall-clock stated.
validity_evidence: Simulator-computed safety predicates; no human agreement study, no real-robot validation.

name: ReGuard control-theoretic guardrail evaluation (From Refusal to Recovery)
modality: LLM agents (Llama-3.x, GPT-4o/4o-mini/GPT-5, Qwen2.5-72B) acting in simulated planar driving, WebArena shopping with a $50 budget, and a backseat-driver advice setting; guardrail trained by safety-critical RL in the model's latent space; scored by success rate, failure (collision/bankruptcy) rate, value F1, intervention rate vs flag-and-block (LlamaGuard) baselines.

Key reused from speaker-bajcsy.json. Level set to 4 on the 0-9 ladder (simulated planar driving and WebArena closed loop; sweeps had 1/4).

name: THE COLOSSEUM
modality: Manipulation models act closed-loop in RLBench/CoppeliaSim on 20 tasks under 14 perturbation axes (colour, texture, size, lighting, distractors, camera pose, physics); binary success.
what_it_measures: Generalization degradation under controlled environmental perturbations, with a real-world check of perturbation effects.

reported_metrics: Success drops 30-50% per perturbation, >=75% with combined perturbations; sim-real correlation of perturbation effects R^2 = 0.614.
cost_evidence: Real validation: 4 tasks, 5 demos each, 2 alternate variations per factor, 10 episodes x 3 runs.
validity_evidence: Moderate R^2=0.614 between sim and real perturbation sensitivities.

name: X2Real

reported_metrics: 0.84 linear correlation between simulated and real-robot evaluation results.
validity_evidence: r = 0.84 sim vs real evaluation.
notes: Abstract only.

name: Drone-Bench
modality: Coding agent (ReAct loop, bash/read/write tools + read_image) is fed office videos, drone poses, obstacle maps and reference images; it writes drone-control code and submits up to 10 times per run; navigate/follow are scored in a MuJoCo model of the office calibrated to a DJI Tello, reconstruct/localize/detect are scored on real recordings on a T4 GPU worker; scores normalised to a human+AI baseline.
what_it_measures: Whether frontier models can autonomously write code for a simple surveillance stack (reconstruction, localisation, navigation, detection, following) on a USD 129 drone; dual-use capability tracking.
size: 5 tasks x 10 runs x 15 models (May 2024 - Jul 2026), 10 submissions per run
reported_metrics: Claude Fable 5 reaches 84% of baseline averaged over tasks (reconstruction 47%); best run clears 4/5 tasks; average end-to-end success ~6% (later reported 2.8% for GPT-6 Astra); ~6-month gap between best-case and average-case; cheating incidents rise from 0.6% (2024 models) to 50.6% (newest).
cost_evidence: Hardware: DJI Tello EDU, USD 129; scoring compute: one NVIDIA T4 per submission with 5 h (reconstruction), 2 h (localisation), 1500 s (detection) timeouts; 120 s wall-clock per simulated flight; real-drone end-to-end runs only for reference solutions and top submissions.
validity_evidence: Sim-to-real alignment checked by running reference and top submissions in both simulator and on the physical Tello and confirming matching behaviour; simulator noise calibrated from physical flight tests. No quantitative sim-real correlation reported.
notes: PDF fetched and text extracted. Hybrid ladder position: level 4 (MuJoCo) for navigate/follow, level 5 (real-data replay) for perception tasks, level 7 end-to-end checks on the physical drone.

validity_evidence: Instruction validity checked automatically only; authors list human-in-the-loop validation as future work.

name: Do open-loop metrics predict closed-loop driving? NAVSIM vs Bench2Drive
modality: Cross-benchmark rank correlation of published NAVSIM PDMS sub-scores against Bench2Drive closed-loop Driving Score for the same end-to-end planners.
what_it_measures: Predictive validity of an open-loop safety score for closed-loop outcomes.

reported_metrics: Spearman rho = 0.90 (PDMS vs Driving Score) but non-monotonic; Ego Progress rho = 0.83 is the best single predictor; No-Collision rho = 0.45; a 3-metric formula matches the 5-metric PDMS; over-cautious planners score high open-loop but underperform closed-loop.
validity_evidence: The clearest quantitative validity estimate found for a cheap driving evaluation predicting a more expensive one; note the collision sub-metric is the weakest predictor.

cost_evidence: Training ~20 h on 8 A100; inference 347 ms at K=10 samples; GPT-4o verification 7-10 s per query.
validity_evidence: none stated beyond simulation success; OOD suite is synthetic perturbation of LIBERO.
notes: Released artifacts: https://github.com/NVlabs/Libero-10-r (fetched 200), dataset on HuggingFace nvidia/libero-r-datasets. Robustness rather than safety benchmark; included because the OOD suite is reusable and released. Level set to 4 on the 0-9 ladder (LIBERO simulation; sweeps had 5).

size: 750 tasks (450 detailed unsafe, 100 abstract unsafe, 200 safe) over 10 hazard types and 3 task types; 9 baselines.

cost_evidence: Mostly CPU experiments; one RTX 4090 for open models via vLLM. Human review of all instructions and goal conditions; annotator count not stated.
validity_evidence: GPT-4o judge vs human consistency 91.89% / 90.36% / 90.70% on the three task types from a 1,008-rating user study. No real-robot validation.
notes: One of the few entries reporting judge-vs-human agreement. v5 Oct 2025. Not adversarial per se (hazardous but sincere instructions); included because it is the standard planner-safety benchmark that jailbreak papers reuse.

name: Parting with Misconceptions (nuPlan open-loop vs closed-loop)
modality: Planners fed nuPlan real-log scenes; scored by open-loop displacement error (OLS) and closed-loop scores with non-reactive and reactive agents (CLS-NR, CLS-R) measuring collisions, drivable area, progress, comfort.

name: NAVSIM
modality: End-to-end driving policy receives real sensor data + ego state from OpenScene/nuPlan; outputs a trajectory; scored by PDM Score (PDMS) computed by non-reactive BEV unrolling over a 4 s horizon at 10 Hz (collision, drivable area, ego progress, TTC, comfort).
what_it_measures: Whether open-loop-style evaluation on real logs can predict closed-loop driving quality; ranks vision-based end-to-end planners on collision/progress/comfort subscores.
size: navtrain 103k samples, navtest 12k samples (after filtering trivial scenes)
reported_metrics: PDMS shows higher Spearman correlation with nuPlan closed-loop score than displacement errors; CVPR 2024 challenge: 143 teams, 463 submissions; TransFuser-style methods match UniAD.
cost_evidence: Non-reactive BEV simulation, no sensor rendering; designed to be cheap enough for large-scale benchmarking (thousands of scenes per evaluation).
validity_evidence: Correlation of PDMS with nuPlan closed-loop score reported in-paper; independent 2026 study (arXiv 2605.00066, not Pavone) finds PDMS strongly but non-monotonically correlated with closed-loop Bench2Drive and Spearman 0.90 for a 3-metric variant.

name: Evaluating Gemini Robotics policies in a Veo world simulator
modality: VLA policy actions condition an action-conditioned, multi-view-consistent Veo video model; 8-second rollouts under nominal, OOD (background, distractors, novel objects) and safety-probe scenes are scored by human evaluators with binary success; sim scores compared with real ALOHA 2 evaluations.
what_it_measures: Whether a generative video world model can rank and score robot policies for nominal performance, OOD generalization and physical/semantic safety as well as real-world evaluation does.
size: 8 Gemini Robotics policy checkpoints; 5 bimanual tasks; 1600+ real-world evaluation episodes for validation.
reported_metrics: Strong linear correlation between predicted and real success rates for nominal tasks; Mean Maximum Rank Violation 0.06 for policy ranking; correlations remain strong for background/distractor shifts; safety failures discovered in the simulator were reproduced on the real robot.
cost_evidence: 1600+ real episodes used as ground truth; human raters score every episode; generative rollouts avoid hardware risk for safety probing; no hours or compute figures stated.
validity_evidence: Sim-vs-real correlation and rank consistency reported against 1600+ real trials; discovered safety failures replicated on hardware.
notes: Sindhwani is a listed author (team paper). Pearson coefficient value not captured from the HTML fetch; the 0.06 MMRV figure is. v2 January 2026. Vikas Sindhwani is a co-author. Only entry in this sweep with explicit safety red-teaming validated on hardware. Key reused from speaker-sindhwani.json (which placed it at level 6; task ladder places generative photoreal simulation at 5). Sindhwani is a co-author. Aliases in sweeps: gemini2025veo, gemini2025veosim. Level set to 5 on the 0-9 ladder (Veo world-model rollouts; validated against 1600+ real ALOHA 2 episodes; sweeps had 5/6).

name: GigaWorld-1 / WMBench
modality: Video world models act as surrogate evaluators; WMBench pairs world-model rollouts with real executions and scores outcome with a VLM; 8 task families.
what_it_measures: How well world models rank policies vs real, and what drives evaluator quality (long-horizon action-faithful consistency over visual realism).
size: 7 world models, 4 action representations, 324k+ rollouts, 2,989 paired real/sim trajectories, 12k+ h video
reported_metrics: Ranking correlation rho=0.61 for Cosmos-Predict2.5 baseline; GigaWorld-1 +14.9% on alignment metric; VLM outcome judge vs human: 87.8% exact agreement, Spearman 0.757.
cost_evidence: 32 NVIDIA H20 GPUs for training; 100+ challenge teams.
validity_evidence: Largest paired real/world-model dataset found; VLM-human agreement quantified.

name: EUVS (Extrapolated Urban View Synthesis Benchmark)

reported_metrics: PSNR drops 23-40% from interpolated to extrapolated views; average degradation >25% across metrics.
cost_evidence: 300+ hours manual traversal selection, 800+ compute hours for COLMAP.
validity_evidence: none stated (image metrics only)

validity_evidence: Correlation with real closed-loop success; PolaRiS reports plain MSE as a low-correlation baseline.

validity_evidence: Compared against closed-loop performance in simulation.

notes: Foundational for the group's 'task-aware evaluation' line. Level set to 5 on the 0-9 ladder (illustrative simulation plus real AV data; sweeps had 1).

name: PolaRiS
org: UW / Stanford / UC Berkeley / TRI / Physical Intelligence
modality: DROID-trained VLAs act closed-loop in interactive sim environments reconstructed (neural reconstruction) from 2-5 minute video scans of real scenes; rollouts scored by humans with the same rubric used for real rollouts.
what_it_measures: Whether real-to-sim environments plus a light co-training recipe give simulated scores that track real-world generalist policy performance across unseen scenes.
size: 6 paired real/sim environments, 6 tasks, 4 policies (pi0, pi0-FAST, PaliGemma-binning, pi0.5); 15 held-out co-training scenes
reported_metrics: Pearson r=0.90 avg with real performance, worst-case r=0.81; r=0.98 vs RoboArena scores; LIBERO scores of the same policies cluster at 90-95% regardless of real performance; Ctrl-World video-model eval MMRV 0.22.
cost_evidence: 20 real rollouts per policy per environment; 50 sim rollouts per task; scene scan 2-5 min, environment build under 1 hour (30 min training + 20 min composition); co-training <25 min, ~350 demos.
validity_evidence: Paired real/sim evaluation across 6 environments; explicitly shows LIBERO saturation gives near-zero discriminative power on real-world ranking, while PolaRiS preserves ranking.
notes: Strong cost and validity evidence in one place.

name: RobotArena Infinity
modality: VLAs act closed-loop in ~100 sim environments auto-reconstructed from demonstration videos (BridgeSim, DROIDSim, RH20TSim) plus perturbations; scored by Gemini 2.5 Pro task-progress on frames + sim state, and by crowdsourced pairwise human preferences.
what_it_measures: Scalable ranking of generalist policies via real-to-sim translation, with VLM progress scores validated against human preferences.
size: ~100 nominal environments (70 BridgeSim) with hundreds of perturbations; 6 VLAs; 8,749 human pairwise preferences
reported_metrics: Human and VLM policy rankings match exactly (6 policies); one task recreated in real to check consistency (qualitative).
cost_evidence: 8,749 crowdworker preference pairs; written justification improved annotation accuracy; per-scene reconstruction cost not stated.
validity_evidence: VLM-vs-human ranking agreement only; sim-vs-real quantified on a single task qualitatively. Weak on real-world validity.

name: RoboWorld (neural simulator eval)
modality: Autoregressive video world model conditioned on policy actions plus task-aware VLM scoring; policies evaluated entirely in the neural simulator; results compared to real-world evaluation.
what_it_measures: Fast, learned-simulator evaluation of generalist policies that preserves real-world rankings.
reported_metrics: Pearson r = 0.989, Spearman rho = 0.970 vs real-world evaluation.
cost_evidence: Claims fast rollouts; no explicit cost numbers in abstract.
validity_evidence: Correlation with real-world evaluation (r=0.989, rho=0.970).
notes: Number of real trials behind the correlation not extracted.

name: Sim2Real Predictivity (Habitat, SRCC)
modality: PointGoal navigation agents receive simulated RGB-D from a 3D-scanned replica of a lab in Habitat; same code runs on a LoCoBot via the Habitat-PyRobot bridge; scored by success and SPL in both.
what_it_measures: Introduces the Sim-vs-Real Correlation Coefficient (SRCC): how well ranking of navigation agents in simulation predicts their real-robot ranking.
size: 9 navigation models tested in parallel in sim and on a LoCoBot in a scanned lab
reported_metrics: SRCC for success under CVPR19 Habitat challenge settings = 0.18; after disabling sliding-along-walls and tuning sim parameters SRCC = 0.844.
cost_evidence: Required 3D scanning of the physical lab and parallel real-robot runs of 9 models; trial counts not stated in abstract.
validity_evidence: Direct: low sim-real correlation traced to agents exploiting simulator collision physics (sliding); predictivity restored by simulator tuning. Earliest quantitative evidence that sim leaderboards can mis-rank real systems.
notes: Navigation, not manipulation, but the SRCC concept is the ancestor of MMRV/Pearson reporting in later work.

name: Waymo Collision Avoidance Testing (CAT)
modality: Scenario-based responder-role tests: the full ADS is fed real sensor logs recorded on a closed test track (increasingly synthetic sensor data), re-simulated closed-loop against new software; scored by collision occurrence and probability of serious injury p(MAIS3+) versus a NIEON (non-impaired, eyes-on) human reference model; a subset of scenarios is physically reproduced on the test track with soft targets and mannequins.
what_it_measures: Whether the ADS meets or exceeds a competent human reference in urgent collision-avoidance scenarios, aggregated by scenario safety group and road-user group.
size: Over 13,000 scenarios for the SF/PHX ODD (48% pedestrian/cyclist conflicts, 52% vehicle); about 70 scenarios reproduced on a test track for each start of fully autonomous operation
reported_metrics: Serious-injury thresholds p(MAIS3+) >= 5% (vehicle-vehicle), >= 1.5% (child pedestrian), >= 10% (other VRU); NIEON reference prevented 84% of serious-injury risk in reconstructed fatal crashes; release-to-release change in aggregate score 1.5% (collision metric) and 0.6% (serious injury metric); 25% (106) of newly observed on-road events were not covered by the existing database and were added.
cost_evidence: Simulation evaluates thousands of scenarios 'within hours instead of months or years' on track; track testing limited to about 70 scenarios per launch because of time and hazard to test staff; synthetic scenarios used where track collection is too dangerous or impractical.
validity_evidence: Simulation-vs-track check: simulations must give a conservative collision count (as many or more simulated collisions than on track) and simulated trajectories must be even with or ahead of track trajectories; qualitative pass only, no correlation coefficient published.
notes: Numbers taken from the full PDF text. Track subset is level 8; the bulk is level 5 (real sensor-data replay).

name: Conformal Decision Theory pedestrian-navigation risk evaluation
modality: Robot planner around pedestrians replayed from the Stanford Drone Dataset (nexus_4 scene); a conformal controller adapts a risk parameter online; scored by safety violations against a 2 m distance threshold and time-to-goal versus aggressive, conservative and ACI baselines.
what_it_measures: Whether decisions calibrated directly by conformal risk control achieve a target long-run risk without distributional assumptions, and at what efficiency cost.
size: One SDD scene (nexus_4) with dense pedestrians; plus stock trading and manufacturing case studies.
reported_metrics: 0 safety violations at learning rate eta>=100; time-to-goal 17.4 s vs ACI 26.67 s (~29% faster) vs unsafe aggressive 8.57 s; min distance 1.142 m.
validity_evidence: Replay of real pedestrian trajectories; statistical risk guarantee is assumption-free but evaluated on a single scene.
notes: Bajcsy equal-contribution co-first author. Adjacent; the evaluation is small. Level set to 5 on the 0-9 ladder (replay of Stanford Drone Dataset pedestrians; sweeps had 3).

name: Learning AV safety concepts from demonstrations
modality: Reasonable-behaviour assumptions learned from highway traffic-weaving demonstrations; safety concept synthesised via HOCBF / HJ reachability; used to evaluate real-world driving logs.
what_it_measures: Which logged interactions violate a data-derived safety concept; comparison with hand-designed concepts (e.g. RSS-like).
reported_metrics: Learned concept evaluates real driving logs; qualitative comparison to baselines.
validity_evidence: none stated

name: SIMPLER (SimplerEnv)
org: UC San Diego / Stanford / UC Berkeley / Google DeepMind
modality: Closed-loop manipulation policy (RT-1, RT-1-X, RT-2-X, Octo) receives simulated RGB observations from SAPIEN/ManiSkill2 with real-to-sim visual matching (real background overlay, texture tuning) or variant aggregation; scored by binary task success.
what_it_measures: Whether simulated success rates and rankings of real-world manipulation policies track their real-robot success rates on Google Robot and WidowX/Bridge tasks.
size: 2 robot setups; Google Robot: pick coke can, move near, open/close drawer; BridgeData V2 tasks; 6 policy checkpoints
reported_metrics: Google Robot: Pearson r=0.924 avg (0.976 pick coke, 0.855 move near, 0.942 drawer); MMRV 0.056 avg; Bridge MMRV 0.143 avg.

validity_evidence: Paired sim/real evaluation of 6 policies: strong Pearson correlation and low rank violation; sim reproduces real behaviour modes such as sensitivity to distribution shift. Later work (Wang et al. 2026 recipe) measured SIMPLER at Spearman 0.40 / Pearson 0.40 on newer VLAs, so validity degrades off the original policy set.
notes: Canonical real-to-sim evaluation paper. MMRV = mean maximum rank violation. Canonical level-4-predicts-level-7 evidence. Level set to 5 on the 0-9 ladder (digital-twin simulation validated against real; sweeps had 4/5).

name: WorldEval (world model as real-world policy evaluator)
modality: Policy2Vec turns a video generation model into a latent-action-following world simulator; policy performance in generated rollouts compared with real-world scenarios; also used as a safety detector for dangerous actions.
what_it_measures: Whether a video world model ranks real robot policies correctly and flags dangerous actions before deployment.
reported_metrics: Strong correlation with real-world performance claimed; outperforms real-to-sim approaches.
cost_evidence: Motivated by cost of real evaluation; no numbers.
validity_evidence: Correlation with real evaluation claimed but coefficient not in abstract.

reported_metrics: none stated

name: InspecSafe-V1 (industrial inspection safety)

reported_metrics: Dataset paper; no model numbers in abstract.

validity_evidence: Labels are practitioner safety levels; no inter-annotator statistics in abstract.
notes: Scientific Data (accepted). Real operational data replayed offline: level 5.

name: JoyAI-Sim
modality: Real tabletop tasks reconstructed as calibrated Isaac Sim digital twins; policy checkpoints evaluated closed-loop; human embodied inspection of motion naturalness.

reported_metrics: Pearson r=0.89, Spearman 0.78 sim vs real success; ~90% of replays reproduce real object-placement outcomes.

validity_evidence: Paired checkpoint evaluation; replay consistency 90%.
notes: 37 authors; industrial system, limited external replication.

name: NeuroNCAP: photorealistic closed-loop safety testing
modality: NeRF reconstruction of real nuScenes logs re-rendered with inserted safety-critical actors (stationary, frontal, side); end-to-end camera planners driven closed-loop; Euro NCAP-inspired 0-5 score from collision avoidance and impact-speed reduction.

validity_evidence: Same open-loop vs closed-loop divergence as dauner2023parting, now with photoreal rendering; no real-vehicle check.

name: From Seeing to Simulating (digital cousins, WorldComposer)
modality: Real panoramas mapped to Isaac Sim scenes plus semantically/geometrically edited cousin scenes; policies (ACT, DP, SmolVLA, pi0) evaluated closed-loop; success rate.
what_it_measures: Sim-to-real correlation of generated scenes and value of cousin-scene data for generalization.
size: 6 tasks (rigid, articulated, deformable/fluid), 4 policies, 20 real trials per configuration
reported_metrics: Pearson r=0.91 sim vs real success; 50 real + 100 sim trajectories reach 0.57 vs 0.33 real-only on unseen scenes.

validity_evidence: Paired evaluation r=0.91; sim failures reported as reliable predictors of real failures.

name: SafeVL (VLM driving-safety evaluator)
modality: Driving video fed to a VLM with object-centric chain-of-thought; outputs collision-prone / safe classification; trained with counterfactual unsafe-scenario generation; tested on Nexar collision dataset and as a critic inside UniAD on NeuroNCAP.

size: Nexar collision dataset (size not stated); NeuroNCAP closed-loop benchmark
reported_metrics: 76% zero-shot accuracy on Nexar (+20% over prior); 8% collision-rate reduction on NeuroNCAP when integrated with UniAD.
validity_evidence: Accuracy vs real dashcam collision labels; closed-loop effect on NeuroNCAP.

name: WorldGym
modality: Policy actions fed to an autoregressive action-conditioned video world model from an initial frame; Monte Carlo rollouts scored by GPT-4o as reward; success rate.
what_it_measures: Whether success in a learned world model predicts real success and preserves policy rankings.
size: 17 Bridge tasks, 3 policies (RT-1-X, Octo, OpenVLA); 510 real trials (10 per task per policy)
reported_metrics: Pearson r=0.78 with real success; mean success differs by 3.3%; GPT-4o judge TPR 0.81, TNR 0.97, FPR 0.03.
cost_evidence: All rollouts under one hour on a single GPU; world model trained 300k steps on 2x A100 80GB.
validity_evidence: Paired real evaluation r=0.78; object-interaction realism remains a limitation.
notes: World-model evaluators placed at level 5 (learned photoreal simulator, closed-loop, no physics engine); see synthesis for the ladder caveat.

name: SimFoundry
modality: Zero-shot real-to-sim scene construction from a video; digital twins and edited variants used for policy training and closed-loop evaluation; success rate.
what_it_measures: Fidelity of automatically generated digital twins as evaluation proxies and as training data.
reported_metrics: Mean Pearson r=0.911 sim-vs-real; MMRV 0.018; cousin-scene training gains 17-40%.

name: STRIVE
modality: Graph-based conditional VAE traffic prior; optimisation in its latent space perturbs a real scene to make a given planner collide, then a second optimisation finds a solution to keep the scenario solvable; scored by collision induction and planner hyperparameter improvements.

reported_metrics: Attacks two planners; scenarios used to tune a rule-based planner.
validity_evidence: none stated

name: REALM
org: CIIRC CTU Prague / University of Amsterdam
modality: DROID-embodiment VLAs (pi0, pi0-FAST, GR00T N1.5) run closed-loop in Isaac Sim with system-identified friction/armature (14 parameters); 15 perturbation factors (6 visual, 8 semantic, 7 behavioural); binary success.

reported_metrics: Sim/real datapoints close to identity, low MMRV, p<0.001; attention-map cosine similarity 0.85 between real and sim frames for pi0. Independent measurement (Wang et al. 2026): Spearman 0.70, Pearson 0.785, MMRV 0.030.
cost_evidence: ~800 paired real/sim rollouts for validation; system identification of 14 parameters.
validity_evidence: Paired real-to-sim validation on unseen scenes; independently confirmed as the best-correlating of three simulators by Wang et al. 2026.

reported_metrics: none stated

name: Confidence-aware game-theoretic safety monitor evaluated on INTERACTION dataset
modality: HJ backward reachable tube (BRT) safety monitor with Bayesian confidence over game-theoretic human models; evaluated in simulated merging/roundabout/highway interactions and by replaying real human driving pairs; scored by safety-controller activation count, reward improvement percent, over-conservatism percentage (BRT area vs least-conservative BRT) and BRT violation percentage on real data.
what_it_measures: How conservative a runtime safety monitor is relative to real human driving, and whether confidence-aware models cut interventions without collisions.
size: 200 pairwise interactions extracted from the INTERACTION dataset; simulated roundabout and highway scenarios; ablations with unmodeled distracted humans.
reported_metrics: ~20% fewer safety-controller activations than full BRT in roundabout while collision-free; +27.75% reward vs full BRT; +9.18% vs lambda-only BRT under misspecification; ~29% reward gain over no-game variant; over-conservatism and violation percentages both significantly reduced vs full BRT on real data.
validity_evidence: Real human driving replays show humans violate the proposed monitor's constraints less often than the full BRT, i.e. the monitor is closer to observed human safety margins.
notes: Bajcsy is equal-contribution co-first author. The real-data conservatism metric (fraction of real interactions a monitor would flag as unsafe) is a reusable proxy evaluation for runtime monitors. Level set to 5 on the 0-9 ladder (simulated interactions plus replay of real INTERACTION-dataset human pairs; sweeps had 4).

name: Interaction-dynamics-aware perception safety zones

size: nuScenes; 4644 false positives analysed; 40x40x20x15x15 state grid
reported_metrics: HJ zone flags 35 safety-critical FPs (0.75%) vs 305 (6.6%) for circular baseline, 8.7x reduction; 4.5 ms per object online, 228 s offline.
cost_evidence: 228 s offline compute, 28.8 MB memory, 4.5 ms per object.
validity_evidence: none stated (theoretical completeness argument)

reported_metrics: Strong positive correlation (coefficients not stated); policies trained on WM data match real-data-trained policies.

name: R2S-Eval
modality: Policies rolled out in real-to-sim calibrated scenes; rollout videos judged pairwise by a VLM; preferences aggregated into rankings.

size: 6 policies (pi0, pi0.5, OpenVLA, NORA-Long, SmolVLA, X-VLA); 7 real tasks; 20 real trials/task; 200 sim trials/task
reported_metrics: Spearman 0.957 and Pearson 0.978 between sim-VLM ranking and hardware ranking; VLM-human agreement 91.9% (real-to-sim) and 82.9% (LIBERO).
cost_evidence: Operator time in conventional evaluation grows ~linearly with trials; R2S-Eval needs hardware only for initial calibration.
validity_evidence: Ranking correlation with hardware and VLM-human agreement both reported.
notes: Very recent preprint (Sept 2026); org unverified.

name: Sim-and-real correlation recipe for VLA evaluation
modality: Five VLAs (pi0, pi0-FAST, pi0.5, GR00T N1.6, N1.7) run closed-loop in three simulators (VLA-Arena/MuJoCo, SIMPLER/SAPIEN, REALM/Isaac Sim) on 9 tabletop tasks aligned with real tasks; sim success compared to real success.
what_it_measures: Which simulators and which simulated signals preserve real-world policy rankings, and whether simulator co-training improves correlation.
size: 9 aligned tasks, 5 policies, 3 simulators; 11,800 sim rollouts and 1,115 real rollouts
reported_metrics: Before post-training: VLA-Arena Spearman 0.575 / Pearson 0.725 / MMRV 0.060; SIMPLER 0.400 / 0.402 / 0.128; REALM 0.700 / 0.785 / 0.030. After sim post-training (REALM): Spearman 0.875, Pearson 0.878, MMRV 0.015.
cost_evidence: 1,115 real rollouts (about 55 real trials and 2,020 sim rollouts per policy-task-perturbation cell).
validity_evidence: Head-to-head comparison of three simulators against the same real data; shows simulator choice changes rank correlation from 0.40 to 0.70, and photoreal Isaac-based REALM outperforms SIMPLER on current VLAs.
notes: Most direct cross-simulator validity comparison found. Abstract only; included because it is a meta-study of exactly the validity question. Aliases in sweeps: wang2026simrealrecipe. Level set to 5 on the 0-9 ladder (sim-real correlation recipe validated against real rollouts; sweeps had 4/5).

cost_evidence: 3D printing of objects; LiDAR/camera capture rig; no figures.
validity_evidence: Physical capture of printed objects confirms evasion; collision rate only in simulation.

Downstream latent safety filter evaluated on hardware.
what_it_measures: Whether a world model's latent state carries the information needed to detect and anticipate safety violations under partial observability (estimation gaps vs prediction gaps), and how much mitigation (multimodal supervision, conformal risk calibration) recovers safety on real cooking-like tasks.
size: 2 hardware tasks on Franka Research 3 (wax heating with IR camera, rice pouring with GelSight tactile); 20 trials per method (wax), 50 filled + 50 empty bottle trials (rice); training data 180 (wax) and 650 (rice) teleop trajectories.

cost_evidence: 20-100 hardware trials per condition; WM training 20k iterations, safety filter 600k DDPG iterations; sensors: FLIR Lepton IR, Intel D415, Zed Mini, GelSight Mini. No wall-clock stated.
validity_evidence: Diagnostics computed offline are shown to predict which sensing configuration yields safe hardware behavior (low MI for RGB matches 15% success; high MI for IR matches 100%). Sample sizes small (20-50 trials) with reported confidence intervals.
notes: arXiv posted Oct 2025; lab page lists CoRL 2026. Project page https://cmu-intentlab.github.io/multisafe/ fetched (200). The diagnostics are reusable as an offline test of whether a safety filter's sensing suite is sufficient.
