validity_evidence: Statistical argument; no sim-real component.

name: Beyond the Patch (viewpoint-consistent 3D adversarial objects)
modality: Adversarial texture on a 3D object optimised via differentiable rendering with EOT and a coarse-to-fine curriculum, with saliency-guided targeted loss that draws the policy toward the object; tested under moving wrist cameras; black-box transfer and real-world demonstration.
what_it_measures: Effectiveness of 3D adversarial objects against visuomotor policies under dynamic viewpoints where 2D patches fail.
reported_metrics: none stated in abstract
validity_evidence: none stated
bibtex: @inproceedings{lee2026beyond, title={Beyond the Patch: Exploring Vulnerabilities of Visuomotor Policies via Viewpoint-Consistent 3D Adversarial Object}, author={Lee, Chanmi and Yoon, Minsung and Kim, Woojae and Lee, Sebin and Yoon, Sung-eui}, booktitle={IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)}, year={2026}}
notes: ICRA 2026 per arXiv comment; details not extracted.

name: AttackVLA (+BackdoorVLA)
modality: Unified framework re-implementing 6 adversarial (PGD, UADA, UPA, TMA, RoboGCG, FreezeVLA) and 3 backdoor (BadVLA, TabVLA, BackdoorVLA) attacks on OpenVLA, SpatialVLA, pi0-fast in LIBERO (4 suites x 10 tasks) and on a 7-DoF Franka with a hand-collected dataset; scored by untargeted failure and targeted ASR.
what_it_measures: Comparable attack effectiveness across VLA architectures and tokenisers, sim and real.
size: 9 attacks x 3 models x 40 LIBERO tasks; 200 real-robot trials
reported_metrics: BackdoorVLA targeted ASR avg 58.4% (75.35% OpenVLA, 51.63% SpatialVLA, 48.23% pi0-fast; 100% on some tasks); real: TMA 42.5%, TabVLA 20%, BackdoorVLA 50% with 60% clean success.
cost_evidence: Franka arm; 200 real trials; no training-time figures.
validity_evidence: Reports sim vs real for the same attacks (attacks weaker on hardware) but no systematic correlation.
bibtex: @article{li2025attackvla, title={AttackVLA: Benchmarking Adversarial and Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models}, author={Li, Jiayu and Zhao, Yunhan and Zheng, Xiang and Xu, Zonghuan and Li, Yige and Ma, Xingjun and Jiang, Yu-Gang}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2511.12149}, year={2025}}
notes: Best single source for cross-attack comparison.

name: Active Real-World Factor-Based Evaluation
modality: Probabilistic surrogate over task factors (object pose, camera viewpoint); sequential experimental design picks real-robot evaluation configurations by information gain.
what_it_measures: Sample-efficient characterization of a policy's performance distribution and failure regions in real hardware evaluation.
reported_metrics: 20-40% fewer trials than random testing for the same characterization.
validity_evidence: none stated
notes: Directly a value-of-information style approach to evaluation design.

name: SafeLoop
modality: Risk predictor + rollback wrapper around a VLA; evaluated on 24 LIBERO tasks (16 seeds) and 3 real-robot tasks with 25 rollouts each; metrics: hazard cases and task success.
what_it_measures: Whether a runtime safety wrapper reduces hazards without hurting success.
size: 24 sim tasks x 16 seeds; 3 real tasks x 25 rollouts
reported_metrics: ~70% reduction in hazard cases with success maintained.
cost_evidence: 25 real rollouts per task (typical scale of academic real-robot safety eval).
validity_evidence: none stated
notes: Included mainly as a data point on trial counts in real-robot safety papers.

name: POEX / Harmful-RLbench
modality: Hidden-layer gradient optimisation produces harmful yet executable policy code; multi-agent evaluator judges jailbroken policies; Harmful-RLbench of human-object-environment risks; simulation and real robots.
what_it_measures: Policy-executable jailbreak success against LLM-based robots (executability as a distinct requirement).
reported_metrics: Not in abstract; shows text-only jailbreaks are inapplicable to robots.
validity_evidence: Multi-agent evaluator; no human agreement in abstract.
notes: v3 Aug 2025.

name: Phantom Menace: physical sensor attacks on VLAs
modality: Real-Sim-Real framework: physics-based camera (6) and microphone (2) attack vectors simulated, then validated on real robots running VLA policies; adversarial training defence.
what_it_measures: Robustness of VLA models to physical sensor attacks.
reported_metrics: Significant vulnerabilities across VLA architectures (rates in body).
validity_evidence: Attacks generated in simulation and confirmed on physical robots.

name: UPA-RFAS (universal transferable patch)
modality: Universal patch optimised on surrogate OpenVLA-7B with feature-space, l1-deviation and repulsive InfoNCE losses plus min-max robustness augmentation; transferred to OpenVLA-OFT variants and pi0 in LIBERO (10 tasks x 10 trials per suite) and to physical executions with pre-set patch sites.
what_it_measures: Cross-model, cross-task, cross-viewpoint transfer of a single physical patch.
size: 100 rollouts per suite per model; physical trials count not stated
reported_metrics: OpenVLA-oft-w success 98.25% -> 5.75% (sim) and -> 40.25% (physical).
cost_evidence: Hardware not specified in fetched text; optimisation hyperparameters given, no wall-clock.
validity_evidence: Again a large sim (5.75%) vs physical (40.25%) success gap.
bibtex: @inproceedings{lu2025uparfas, title={When Robots Obey the Patch: Universal Transferable Patch Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models}, author={Lu, Hui and Yu, Yi and Yang, Yiming and Yi, Chenyu and Zhang, Qixin and Shen, Bingquan and Kot, Alex C. and Jiang, Xudong}, booktitle={IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)}, year={2026}}
notes: CVPR 2026.

name: Online distribution-shift detection via recency prediction
modality: Streaming high-dimensional observations; detector with guaranteed false-positive rate; evaluated in simulation and hardware visual servoing.
what_it_measures: Detection speed and false-positive guarantee of a runtime distribution-shift monitor.
reported_metrics: Up to 11x faster detection than prior work; alerts issued before failure on hardware.
validity_evidence: Alert precedes failure on hardware.
bibtex: @inproceedings{luo2022recency, title={Online Distribution Shift Detection via Recency Prediction}, author={Luo, Rachel and Sinha, Rohan and Sun, Yixiao and Hindy, Ali and Zhao, Shengjia and Savarese, Silvio and Schmerling, Edward and Pavone, Marco}, booktitle={IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)}, year={2024}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.09916}}
notes: Venue ICRA 2024 per arXiv comments; runtime-monitor evaluation.

name: Sim2Val
modality: Paired measurements of the same scenario on a cheap platform (simulator / open-loop playback) and the expensive target platform (closed-loop or real vehicle); real-world metric mean estimated with control variates.
what_it_measures: How many real-world test samples are needed for a confidence bound on a safety/performance metric when correlated cheap proxies exist; variance reduction of the estimator.
size: nuPlan: 565 real + 1320 surrogate samples; real AV: 138 intersection / 75 curve events paired with 781 / 423 neural-reconstruction sim runs; quadruped: 200 real + 400 sim
reported_metrics: Variance reduction 22-35% (nuPlan ADE), 82.9% (real AV closest-distance), 5.9% (quadruped, rho=0.07); 51% fewer paired samples for same CI in one domain; sim-real correlation rho>0.9 for AV logs vs 0.07 for quadruped.
cost_evidence: Cost ratios between platforms formalised (budget allocation in appendix); real AV logs and quadruped hardware used; no dollar figures.
validity_evidence: Method's benefit is itself a function of measured sim-to-real correlation; reports rho per platform.
bibtex: @inproceedings{luo2025sim2val, title={Sim2Val: Leveraging Correlation Across Test Platforms for Variance-Reduced Metric Estimation}, author={Luo, Rachel and Yang, Heng and Watson, Michael and Sharma, Apoorva and Veer, Sushant and Schmerling, Edward and Pavone, Marco}, booktitle={Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL)}, year={2025}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20553}}
notes: Closest existing work to a value-of-information framing of evaluation cost; must-cite. Level set to 7 on the 0-9 ladder (quadruped hardware plus real AV test-fleet logs paired with sim; sweeps had 6).

name: X4Val
modality: Non-paired heterogeneous evaluation data (simulation, older policy logs, other regions) embedded with DINO features; learned predictor of real-world metric used as a control variate for the target policy's real-world evaluation.
what_it_measures: Variance-reduced estimation of real-world policy metrics when only unpaired auxiliary data exists (e.g. geographic transfer US to Germany, iterative policy versions).
size: Driving: 200 paired target samples plus 5x1000 samples from earlier policies and 86,848 scenario-only samples; manipulation: 5000 ManiSkill rollouts + 100 real Franka rollouts
reported_metrics: Up to 38.4% variance reduction (iterative development), 15-20% (geographic transfer); consistent reduction on Franka block stacking.
cost_evidence: Real Franka Panda rollouts (100) vs 5000 sim rollouts; NVIDIA PhysicalAI-AV dataset; no hours or dollars stated.
validity_evidence: Reports variance reduction against Monte Carlo on real data; no external ground truth on safety outcomes.
bibtex: @article{luo2026x4val, title={X4Val: Learning Neural Surrogates for Variance-Reduced Policy Evaluation}, author={Luo, Rachel and Watson, Michael and Sharma, Apoorva and Yang, Heng and Qi, Han and Schmerling, Edward and Veer, Sushant and Ivanovic, Boris and Pavone, Marco}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2606.05159}, year={2026}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05159}}
notes: Follow-up to Sim2Val; preprint. Level set to 7 on the 0-9 ladder (100 real Franka rollouts plus real driving logs; sweeps had 6).

name: MuTRAP / Robo-Troj (multi-trigger backdoor on LLM task planners)
modality: Soft-prompt-tuned LLM task planner receives text task requests with/without optimised trigger words; output plans scored for attack success rate (malicious plan emitted) and clean-data accuracy in VirtualHome; demonstration on a UR5e arm.
what_it_measures: Backdoor vulnerability of LLM-based robot task planners: ASR when triggered, benign accuracy otherwise, and false-trigger rate.
size: 7 LLM architectures (GPT2-Large, GPT-J-6B, Llama-2-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, ...); 6 VirtualHome household tasks; 1-10 triggers
reported_metrics: ASR 97-100% across LLMs (98.6-100% for 1/2/5 triggers); clean accuracy 99-100%; trigger optimisation cuts false-trigger rate 71.6% -> 2.5% at 10 triggers.
cost_evidence: Real-world demo on UR5e with gripper; simulation in VirtualHome; no time/dollar figures.
validity_evidence: none stated
bibtex: @inproceedings{nahian2025mutrap, title={MuTRAP: Multi-trigger Trojans Attacking Robot Task Planning Systems}, author={Al Nahian, Mohaiminul and Altaweel, Zainab and Reitano, David and Ahmed, Sabbir and Zhang, Shiqi and Rakin, Adnan Siraj}, booktitle={IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)}, year={2026}}
notes: arXiv v1 titled Robo-Troj; renamed MuTRAP in the IROS 2026 version.

name: Regret metric for system-level prediction failures (Not All Errors Are Made Equal)
modality: Closed-loop human-robot interaction logs (predictor + planner) scored offline by a probabilistic, calibrated regret: the gap between the planner's realized closed-loop performance and what it would have achieved with the true human trajectory. Compared to open-loop ADE/FDE and other system-level metrics.
what_it_measures: Which trajectory-prediction errors actually degraded closed-loop robot behavior (system-level failures), and whether mining high-regret interactions is predictive of re-deployment performance improvement after fine-tuning.
size: 96 closed-loop 20-second driving scenarios (BITS simulator, nuScenes-initialized, AgentFormer predictor, TPP planner): 20 high-regret, 76 low-regret. Hardware: LoCoBot social navigation with a VQ-VAE generative planner trained on 10k synthetic trajectories.
reported_metrics: Generalized regret has 95% overlap with canonical regret but only 35% overlap with ADE-flagged failures; fine-tuning on the 23% high-regret subset gives -65% collision cost and -53% closed-loop regret on high-regret scenarios, competitive with full-data fine-tuning; ADE/FDE 0.327/1.520 vs base 0.371/1.919; hardware regret 0.307 on near-collision vs 0.053-0.078 nominal.
cost_evidence: 96 simulated scenarios and a small number of hardware trials; fine-tuning on 23% of data matches full-data fine-tuning (data efficiency claim). No compute hours stated.
validity_evidence: Presence of high-regret data during fine-tuning is 'highly predictive' of re-deployment improvement; hardware trials show high regret on interactions with unexpectedly close human-robot proximity. Correlation with actual collisions is shown through collision-cost reduction, not accident statistics.
notes: Semantic Scholar also lists a 2024 arXiv title 'A General Calibrated Regret Metric for Detecting and Mitigating Human-Robot Interaction Failures'; this appears to be an earlier version title of the same arXiv ID (v1-v4), not a separate paper. Project page https://cmu-intentlab.github.io/not-all-errors/ and code fetched (200). Level set to 7 on the 0-9 ladder (96 sim scenarios plus LoCoBot hardware re-deployment; sweeps had 6).

name: Latent Safety Filters (latent-space HJ reachability) hardware protocol
modality: RGB observations through a generative world model; failure set specified as a latent-space classifier trained on mixed-quality data (successes, random exploration, unsafe demos); filter shields arbitrary policies (IL and teleop) on a Franka Research 3; scored by prevented failures (bag spilling, toppling clutter) in simulation and hardware.
what_it_measures: Whether a learned latent reachability filter prevents hard-to-specify failures on a real manipulator while preserving task completion.
size: Simulation and hardware experiments; 7 tables and 9 figures per arXiv comment; trial counts not extracted.
reported_metrics: not extracted
validity_evidence: Hardware demonstrations; no large-n statistics in abstract.
notes: Foundational method paper for the latent-safety line; included for context only. Code https://kensukenk.github.io/latent-safety/ fetched (200). Bajcsy link; related CoRL 2025 UNISafe and AnySafe papers use the same Franka hardware. Level set to 7 on the 0-9 ladder (Franka Research 3 hardware; sweeps had 6/7).

name: SafeGate: ISO 13482-grounded pre-execution safety gate for LLM-controlled robots
modality: Natural-language commands to an LLM robot controller are parsed into ISO 13482-derived safety properties and passed through a deterministic accept/reject gate plus task safety contracts (invariants, guards, aborts); scored by acceptance of defective vs benign commands on a text benchmark, in AI2-THOR, and on a real robot.
what_it_measures: Rejection rate of unsafe commands and acceptance rate of benign ones before any physical execution.
size: 230 benchmark tasks, 30 AI2-THOR scenarios, real-robot experiments
reported_metrics: Significantly reduced acceptance of defective commands while keeping high acceptance of benign tasks (numbers not in abstract).
validity_evidence: Text-level gate checked on simulation and hardware, but no agreement statistics reported in abstract.
notes: Spans levels 0, 4 and 7; primary scoring is text-level, hence level 0. Links the physical-safety standard to the LLM-planner end of the ladder. Follow-up to SafePlan. Level set to 7 on the 0-9 ladder (text-level scoring plus AI2-THOR and real-robot experiments; highest rung evaluated; sweeps had 0/7).

name: Open X-Embodiment
modality: Pooled teleoperated/scripted demonstrations from 22 robot embodiments in a common format; RT-X models trained and evaluated across labs.
what_it_measures: Scale of multi-lab real-robot data pooling and cross-embodiment transfer.
reported_metrics: Positive transfer of RT-X across embodiments.
cost_evidence: Aggregates years of collection across 21 institutions; no dollar figure.
validity_evidence: n/a

name: Coverage-Aware Active Evaluation (paired systems)
modality: Cheap proxy system (open-loop playback, lower-fidelity sim, related policy) sampled densely; target system (closed-loop sim, second sim, real Unitree Go2, real KITTI) evaluated under a small budget; scenario selection via residual-corrected risk predictor plus support-aware mutual information.
what_it_measures: Number and diversity of severe target-system failures found under a fixed test budget when proxy evaluations are available.
size: Budgets: nuPlan 170 target evals, SIMPLER 70, quadruped 30 real trials; KITTI perception transfer
reported_metrics: Up to 2x more failures discovered than random and active-learning baselines, including severe/diverse failures missed by baselines.
cost_evidence: Explicit small target budgets (30-170 evaluations) with proxy evaluations treated as cheap; real Unitree Go2 hardware.
validity_evidence: Failures found on real hardware and real KITTI data, not just sim; no predictive validity vs field incidents.
bibtex: @article{parashar2026coverage, title={Coverage Aware Active Evaluation for Failure Discovery with Paired Systems}, author={Parashar, Anjali and Luo, Rachel and Sharma, Apoorva and Veer, Sushant and Schmerling, Edward and Sobolewski, Carson and Yu, Mingxin and Fan, Chuchu and Pavone, Marco}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.13719}, year={2026}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13719}}
notes: Directly about allocating limited real-world test budget; preprint.

name: MANIGUARD
modality: LTLf automaton monitors over physics predicates score foundation-model manipulation policies on 200 locked base tasks (1,000 scenarios with shifts) in simulation and on a physical Franka; 8,000 safety-annotated demos (40 per task) for improvement.
what_it_measures: Specification-grounded safety of manipulation policies, independent of task success.
size: 200 base tasks, 1,000 scenarios, 8,000 demos, 6 task families.
reported_metrics: 6-21% of successful rollouts violate the specification; fine-tuning raises safe completion to 7.5-29.8%.
cost_evidence: 8,000 demos via motion planning plus human teleoperation; no hours stated.
validity_evidence: Automated monitors rather than learned judges; physical Franka evaluation; no human-agreement study.

name: LIBERO-VIFO
modality: Visual cues (8 families) placed in LIBERO scenes; Part I tests authorised cue following, Part II unauthorised cue following under language-cue conflict and empty language; 7 VLAs; extended to safety-critical settings and real robot.
what_it_measures: Whether VLAs execute tasks indicated by unauthorised visual cues (a prompt-injection-like risk).
reported_metrics: Models execute cue-indicated tasks without language instruction (numbers not in abstract).
validity_evidence: Real-robot deployment reported; no human study.

name: RoboGuard
modality: Two-stage guardrail: root-of-trust LLM grounds safety rules into temporal-logic specs from the scene graph; control synthesis rejects/repairs unsafe LLM plans. Evaluated with RoboPAIR-style jailbreak prompts on a Clearpath Jackal in simulation (indoor/outdoor, ~20,000 m^2) and real world; metric is attack success rate (ASR).
what_it_measures: Reduction in executed unsafe plans under worst-case jailbreaks without loss of safe-plan performance.
size: 70 adversarial prompts (7 harmful behaviours x 10 rephrasings) + 10 safe behaviours; >1,500 evaluations across attack variants.
reported_metrics: Unguarded ASR 92.3% +/- 4.7%; with RoboGuard <3%; uses 12-21% of attacker tokens and 1 LLM query vs attacker's 15.
cost_evidence: Onboard compute Nvidia A4000 + Ryzen 5 3600 on the Jackal; token and query counts reported; no hours stated.
validity_evidence: ASR is judged by whether the robot executes the target behaviour; no human-agreement study; controlled-lab real robot only.
notes: IEEE RA-L accepted Feb 2026; v2 March 2026. Code: github.com/KumarRobotics/RoboGuard. Accepted IEEE RA-L 2026 per arXiv PDF header. Included as the paired defense-side evaluation of RoboPAIR.

name: CORE (contextual safety reasoning and grounding)
modality: VLM continuously infers context-dependent safety rules from images, grounds them spatially, and enforces safe sets with control barrier functions; simulation and real-world experiments in unseen environments.
what_it_measures: Runtime enforcement of semantically derived safety constraints on a real robot.
reported_metrics: Not in abstract.
validity_evidence: None stated.

name: RoboPAIR (Jailbreaking LLM-Controlled Robots)
modality: Attacker LLM iteratively rewrites text prompts (with a syntax-checker LLM) sent to the robot's LLM planner; output is a robot API program; scored by an LLM judge (1-10) plus two expert human annotators confirming each jailbreak; the harmful action is then executed on the robot.
what_it_measures: Attack success rate (ASR) of eliciting harmful physical actions (block emergency exit, find weapons, collide with people) from LLM-controlled robots under white-, gray- and black-box access.
size: 3 robots x 7 harmful actions x 5 trials = 35 attempts per method per robot; K=10 attack iterations
reported_metrics: RoboPAIR ASR 100% (35/35) on all three targets; baselines: direct prompt 3-14%, template 86-94%, PAIR 14-49%.
cost_evidence: Hardware: NVIDIA Dolphins (white-box self-driving LLM), Clearpath Jackal UGV with GPT-4o planner, Unitree Go2 with GPT-3.5. K=10 query iterations per attack; no wall-clock or dollar figures.
validity_evidence: LLM judge outputs double-checked by two expert human annotators for every jailbreak; no inter-rater statistic reported. Jailbroken plans physically executed, so harm is observed rather than inferred.
bibtex: @article{robey2024robopair, title={Jailbreaking LLM-Controlled Robots}, author={Robey, Alexander and Ravichandran, Zachary and Kumar, Vijay and Hassani, Hamed and Pappas, George J.}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2410.13691}, year={2024}}
notes: Later appeared at ICRA 2025 (IEEE Xplore). White-box target Dolphins is an NVIDIA/Pavone-group driving LLM, which is the only indirect Pavone link. Ladder level is 7 for the Jackal/Go2 executions; the Dolphins setting is level 0-2 (text/video QA). Project page robopair.org. Dolphins setting is text/video QA (level 0-2); Go2/Jackal are level 7. Aliases in sweeps: robey2024jailbreaking.

name: ArmnetBench v0.1
modality: Policies (fine-tuned on 50 demos/task) run in isolated containers on a farm of SO-101 cells (3 cameras, Raspberry Pi, networked power plug); every rollout labelled success/suboptimal/failure; single-arm and bimanual.
what_it_measures: Parallel, low-cost real-world evaluation of manipulation policies with released labelled rollouts.
size: 12 tasks, 7 policies, 2518 policy rollouts + 600 reference demos (3118 labelled episodes; 3718 released)
reported_metrics: Per-policy success/suboptimal/failure rates across 12 tasks (numbers in paper).
cost_evidence: SO-101 arm BOM ~USD 122 per follower arm (see so-arm100 entry); 'light on-site supervision'; per-trial cost reduced by parallel cells; explicit dollar/hour figures not in abstract.
validity_evidence: Three-way human labels released; no agreement statistics in abstract.
notes: Cheapest hardware per evaluation cell in the catalogue.

name: UNISafe OOD-failure evaluation of latent safety filters
modality: Vision-based control (RGB) through a latent world model; safety filter classifies states safe/unsafe with epistemic uncertainty (Jensen-Renyi divergence) calibrated by conformal prediction; scored by TPR/TNR/balanced accuracy vs ground-truth failure sets, and by failure rate, safe-success rate, incompletion rate in closed loop, including replayed failure trajectories on hardware.
what_it_measures: Whether a latent safety filter detects both known and unseen (OOD) hazards, and the safety/conservativeness tradeoff versus baselines (LatentSafe, SafeOnly, CQL/COMBO, density estimation, total uncertainty).
size: Dubins car: 181 challenging initial states, 1000 safe + 50 random training trajectories. IsaacLab block plucking: 1000 sampled initial conditions, 3000 training trajectories. Hardware Jenga (Franka Research 3): 720 training trajectories (150 random, 480 success, 90 failure), 50 replayed failure trajectories.
reported_metrics: Block plucking: UNISafe safe-success 0.72, failure 0.20, incompletion 8% vs LatentSafe 0.68/0.30/1% vs no filter 0.58/0.41.
cost_evidence: Trajectory counts above; DDQN/SAC solvers; no compute hours stated. Code and IsaacLab demo released.
validity_evidence: Grid-based ground-truth reachability on Dubins car; hardware failure replays only (50), not statistically large.
notes: Method paper; included because the OOD-failure replay protocol and metrics are explicit and code is public (https://cmu-intentlab.github.io/UNISafe/, fetched 200). Level set to 7 on the 0-9 ladder (IsaacLab plus Franka Research 3 Jenga hardware; sweeps had 6).

name: Butter-Bench
modality: LLM is the high-level planner of a TurtleBot4/robot-vacuum with lidar+camera; receives images and a discrete action API (go forward, rotate, navigate to coordinate, capture picture, Slack messaging); scored by human-judged completion of 6 subtasks, 5 trials per task, 15 min limit for end-to-end.
what_it_measures: Practical intelligence of frontier LLMs embodied in a real mobile robot: search, visual inference, social interaction, multi-step spatial planning, end-to-end 'pass the butter'.
size: 6 subtasks x 5 trials x 7 models (Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Opus 4.1, GPT-5, Gemini ER 1.5, Grok 4, Llama 4 Maverick, ...)
reported_metrics: Best LLM 40% (Gemini 2.5 Pro) vs mean human 95%; fine-tuning for embodied reasoning did not help; models struggled most on multi-step spatial planning and social understanding.
cost_evidence: Hardware: TurtleBot 4 Standard (iRobot Create 3 base, ~USD 2k class); 5 trials/task, human operator resets and scoring; no hours or dollar figure stated.
validity_evidence: Human baseline (95%) as reference; qualitative safety/privacy probes (low-battery 'existential' transcripts, Claude sharing a blurry confidential screen image, GPT-5 disclosing laptop location). No correlation with deployment outcomes.
notes: arXiv abstract and Andon Labs eval page both fetched. Cost of a single evaluation run not stated; each trial is human-supervised.

name: AESOP (Real-Time Anomaly Detection and Reactive Planning with LLMs)
modality: Fast binary anomaly classifier in LLM embedding space triggers slow generative-LLM fallback selection; MPC keeps the robot safe during LLM latency; 500 randomised quadrotor simulations plus physical drone experiments.
what_it_measures: Runtime detection of semantic out-of-distribution failures and safe recovery under latency and compute constraints.
size: 500 randomised simulation scenarios; hardware quadrotor demos.
reported_metrics: 100% recovery in simulation vs 77-85% crash/failure for latency-ignoring baselines (per project summary); fast classifier beats autoregressive GPT reasoning even with small LMs.
cost_evidence: Explicit latency budget analysis; no dollars or hours.
validity_evidence: Hardware confirmation of recovery; no human-agreement or field data.
notes: RSS 2024. The 100%/77-85% figures come from a search summary, not the abstract; treat as medium. Method paper; evaluation protocol partly reusable.

name: Policy comparison with near-optimal stopping
modality: Sequential hypothesis test for comparing two imitation policies from binary outcomes; adaptive stopping without p-hacking.
what_it_measures: Minimal number of real trials to decide which of two policies is better with controlled error.
reported_metrics: Up to 32% fewer trials than baselines; >160 sim rollouts saved in a multi-task case.
cost_evidence: Trial savings quantified; adopted by the TRI LBM study.
validity_evidence: none stated

name: Beyond Binary Success (SAVI policy comparison)
modality: Safe anytime-valid inference for sequential policy comparison on binary, partial-credit, reward and smoothness metrics; sim and real data.
what_it_measures: Evaluation burden reduction from fine-grained metrics and sequential testing.
reported_metrics: Up to 70% fewer trials than batch testing; up to 50% fewer than binary sequential methods.
validity_evidence: none stated

name: Q-DIG (quality-diversity red teaming of VLAs)
modality: Quality-diversity search with VLMs generates diverse adversarial instructions for VLAs across simulation benchmarks; real-world checks of generated prompts.
what_it_measures: Instruction-space fragility of VLAs and fine-tuning gains from adversarial prompts.
reported_metrics: Real-world evaluations consistent with simulation (no numbers in abstract).
validity_evidence: Sim-to-real consistency claimed qualitatively.
notes: safety_focus false: robustness/task success.

name: Safe-stoppability monitors for humanoids (PRISM)
modality: Simulation-trained neural predictor of whether a humanoid state admits a safe stop under a fallback balance controller; importance sampling refines decision boundary at rare states; deployed on real humanoid hardware.
what_it_measures: Certifiable fail-safe (emergency stop) behaviour for actively balancing robots.
reported_metrics: Fewer false-safe predictions under fixed sim budget; sim-to-real deployment.
cost_evidence: Simulation budget framed as the constraint; hardware trials not counted in abstract.
validity_evidence: False-safe rate under fixed simulation budget; real deployment demo.

name: 3D collision-force map for safe human-robot collaboration
modality: UR10e and KUKA LBR iiwa driven into an impact measuring device at many workspace positions and speeds; measured impact force compared with the ISO/TS 15066 mass-velocity-force formula.
what_it_measures: Spatial variation of impact force and accuracy of the standard's predictive formula.
reported_metrics: Impact forces vary by more than 100% within the workspace; the ISO/TS 15066 formula both significantly underestimates and overestimates safe speeds; clamping never occurred with the UR10e.
validity_evidence: The analytical (level-0-like) limit computation is a poor predictor of measured force: both false alarms and misses.

name: Effect of protective soft skins on collision forces (2,250 measurements)
org: Czech Technical University / Blue Danube Robotics
modality: UR10e, KUKA LBR iiwa and KUKA Cybertech with and without AIRSKIN active/passive skin collide with a force measurement device; force evolution recorded across impact direction, velocity, stop settings and reaction strategy.
what_it_measures: Transient collision force reduction from passive padding and active skin stops, relative to ISO/TS 15066 limits.
reported_metrics: Passive skin lowers impact forces by about 40%; up to four times the ISO/TS 15066 prescribed velocity can still comply with force limits in some configurations.
cost_evidence: Trial count (2,250) is the best proxy for the hardware cost of a thorough PFL characterisation.
validity_evidence: Shows the standard's velocity limits are conservative by up to 4x for padded robots, i.e. a high false-alarm rate of the analytic rule.

name: SO-100 / SO-101 arm bill of materials
org: The Robot Studio / Hugging Face LeRobot

reported_metrics: n/a

name: TRI Large Behavior Models: careful examination
modality: Diffusion-policy LBMs vs single-task baselines on bimanual Franka FR3 stations; blind, randomised A/B rollouts; binary success via sequential hypothesis testing, Bayesian Beta posteriors, Welch t-tests with Bonferroni, compact letter display.
what_it_measures: Whether multitask pretraining helps, with enough trials to make statistically defensible claims.
size: 1800 real-world rollouts (50 per task/policy/condition, 8 real tasks), >47000 sim rollouts (200 per condition, 24 sim tasks); ~1700 h training data
reported_metrics: Multi-task pretraining improves success/robustness and needs ~80% less data for new skills; ~50 real trials per condition needed to separate policies.
cost_evidence: 1800 real rollouts at 50/condition; 9 robot stations for data collection; 468 h in-house teleop data; explicit statement that most studies lack sufficient trials.
validity_evidence: Statistical framework with explicit power; blind A/B mitigates evaluator bias.
notes: Best single source for 'how many real trials does a defensible comparison need'.

name: Statistical lower bounds for BC policy performance
modality: Visuomotor policies rolled out in sim and on hardware; stochastic-ordering bounds on the full performance CDF with user-specified confidence from a minimal number of rollouts.
what_it_measures: How many rollouts are needed for trustworthy, worst-case performance bounds and OOD comparisons.
reported_metrics: Tight lower bounds validated empirically; open-source code and data.
cost_evidence: Explicitly targets minimal number of hardware rollouts; counts in paper body.
validity_evidence: Bounds hold at stated confidence in simulation; hardware generalisation measured.

name: Adversarial vulnerabilities of VLAs (UADA/UPA/TMA patches)
org: Rochester Institute of Technology / Rutgers et al.
modality: Optimised adversarial patches placed in the camera view of OpenVLA in LIBERO (40 tasks x 50 trials) with untargeted (action discrepancy, position-aware) and targeted objectives; scored by task failure / target-trajectory success; printed patch tested on a UR10e with a webcam.
what_it_measures: Degradation of VLA task success under visual patch attacks in sim and on hardware.
size: LIBERO 4 suites x 10 tasks x 50 trials (2,000 rollouts per setting); 100 real-robot rollouts
reported_metrics: UADA up to 100% failure; UPA 89.7% average failure; TMA 100% in sim; 43% ASR over 100 real trials.
cost_evidence: UR10e + Robotiq Hand-E, single RGB webcam; compute not stated.
validity_evidence: Sim ASR (near 100%) vs physical ASR (43%) shows a large sim-to-real gap for patch attacks.

reported_metrics: Physical ASR ~35% (permutation), ~56% (stagnation), ~44% (intentional); clean accuracy 50-59%.

name: Partially observable patch attacks on VLAs
org: University of Science and Technology of China / Guangzhou University
modality: Patch optimised from a short trajectory prefix, localised via attention maps, then fixed for all later frames; OpenVLA variants and Hume in LIBERO (40 tasks x 100 trials); 18x18 cm printed patch on a ROKAE xMate ER7 Pro with Robotiq 2F-85 and RealSense D455.
what_it_measures: Attack effectiveness under a realistic threat model where the attacker sees only the start of the episode.
size: 4,000 sim rollouts per model; 2 real tasks x 50 trials
reported_metrics: Sim ASR up to 90.7%; real: success 72% -> 12% (task A) and 58% -> 8% (task B).
cost_evidence: Hardware listed above; patch printed at 18 cm; compute not stated.

name: Ontology-based identification of perception triggering conditions (SOTIF)
modality: Ontologies of triggering sources and perception stages generate candidate triggering conditions; a subset is executed with an L3 vehicle in field tests and scored by whether risky behaviour results.

validity_evidence: Analysis-level candidates confirmed on hardware at 40%; the remainder are false alarms at the analysis level or untested.

name: DropVLA (action-level backdoor)
modality: Pipeline-black-box data poisoning (0.31% of episodes) with window-consistent relabelling so a visual trigger forces an action primitive (e.g. open_gripper) at chosen decision points; OpenVLA-7B on LIBERO; physical check with pi0-fast on a 7-DoF Franka.
what_it_measures: Fine-grained action-level backdoor ASR, clean retention, trigger latency and cross-suite transfer under minimal poisoning.
reported_metrics: Vision-only ASR 98.67-99.83%, clean retention 98.50-99.17%; trigger within 25 steps at 500 Hz; cross-suite 96.27-99.09%; text-only 0.72%.

name: BadRobot
org: Huazhong University of Science and Technology et al.
modality: Voice/text malicious queries (277-query benchmark, 7 harm categories) fed to embodied LLM frameworks (VoxPoser, Code as Policies, ProgPrompt, Visual Programming) over GPT-3.5/4/4o, Yi-vision, LLaVA; outputs (language and action code) scored by GPT-4 judge harmfulness 1-5; manipulation success rate (MSR) measured; subset executed on real arms.
what_it_measures: Whether embodied LLM agents can be jailbroken into harmful physical manipulation via three vulnerabilities: contextual jailbreak, safety misalignment (say no, do yes), and conceptual deception.
size: 277 malicious queries; 77 RLBench subtasks for benign capability; real-world trials on UR3e and myCobot 280-Pi
reported_metrics: Contextual jailbreak avg MSR 83% (baseline 25%); safety misalignment 66%; conceptual deception 65%; real-world avg MSR 68.57% vs 22.85% for direct malicious queries.
cost_evidence: Hardware: UR3e and myCobot 280-Pi with Orbbec Gemini 335L RGB-D. Appendix references a cost analysis but no figures visible in the fetched text.
validity_evidence: GPT-4 automated harmfulness judge following Qi et al. 2023; no human-agreement statistic found in fetched text.

name: RedVLA (Physical Red Teaming for VLAs)
modality: Risk objects (knives, obstacles) inserted into LIBERO scenes near critical interaction regions, then gradient-free optimisation of placement; unsafe outcomes detected by binary predicates (state-, cumulative- and conditional-level safety costs); validated on a Franka arm.

reported_metrics: ASR up to 95.5% (pi0.5), 93.2% (pi0), 90.5% (OpenVLA-OFT), 64.9% (OpenVLA) within 10 iterations; real-robot ASR >80% over 10 trials per task.
cost_evidence: Franka hardware; 10 optimisation iterations; compute not reported; human annotation pipeline (Appendix F) for scene plausibility.
validity_evidence: Sim-found risks reproduce on hardware at >80% ASR; scene plausibility human-checked; no inter-annotator statistics in fetched text.

name: AutoEval
modality: Policies submitted to a queue run on WidowX (BridgeData) stations; success judged by fine-tuned VLM classifiers (~1000 labelled images per scene), scenes reset by learned reset policies; outputs success rates and rankings.

reported_metrics: Pearson r = 0.942 and MMRV = 0.015 vs human-run oracle evaluations; classifier >95% accuracy on held-out images; 3 human interventions in 24 h across ~850 episodes.

size: BadLIBERO dataset (size not stated); OpenVLA and VLA-Adapter
reported_metrics: Backdoor goal achieved on 97% of triggered inputs (up to 98% sim, 100% real per project page); zero clean degradation; trigger size has little effect, colour matters.
validity_evidence: none stated

name: Swiss Re / Stanford ADAS proving-ground assessment
modality: Physical vehicles (12 production models MY2022-23 + 1 prototype) driven on a Euro NCAP-accredited proving ground through safety-critical scenarios selected from insurer accident databases; scored by predicted real-world collision-frequency and impact-energy reduction weighted by scenario relevance; realism metric on tested scenarios.
what_it_measures: Relative real-world safety benefit of collision-prevention systems across vehicles; realism of the scenario protocol.
size: 13 vehicles; average 81 tests per vehicle (range 41-161; 18-72% of full matrix); 8-month campaign
reported_metrics: All tested scenarios score as highly realistic (mean realism 0.0024, sd 0.0012 on a nondimensional scale); pre-release prototype outperforms production vehicles in most scenarios.
cost_evidence: Eight-month track campaign at an accredited proving ground in Germany with 13 vehicles; roughly 1000 physical test runs; insurer-funded.
validity_evidence: Scoring explicitly ties to predicted real-world collision frequency; realism metric validates scenario plausibility; no post-hoc comparison to field claims yet.

name: Euro NCAP AEB Car-to-Car test protocol v4.3
modality: Production vehicle driven by a steering/pedal robot toward a Global Vehicle Target (GVT, radar/lidar/camera-representative soft car) on a dry >0.9 PBC track; scenarios CCRs (stationary), CCRm (moving), CCRb (braking), plus crossing/head-on; scored on impact-speed reduction and FCW timing per speed/overlap grid cell; measurement accuracy 0.1 km/h speed, 0.03 m position.
what_it_measures: AEB/FCW avoidance and mitigation performance over a speed x overlap grid (CCRs 10-50 km/h AEB, 55-80 km/h FCW; CCRm 30-80 km/h).
size: Manufacturer supplies a colour-coded prediction for every grid cell; lab tests all grid points if no prediction is supplied, stepping 10 km/h then 5 km/h around first contact
reported_metrics: none stated
cost_evidence: Euro NCAP FAQ: a full test programme 'costs several hundreds of thousands of Euros'; typically a minimum of six test vehicles, one dedicated to ADAS track testing; dummies and targets are expensive and need regular maintenance. Only equipment on the TB029 supplier list may be used. Manufacturer must supply a dossier including HiL/SiL/ViL validation evidence and field false-positive evidence for head-on functions.
validity_evidence: Grid predictions from the OEM are spot-checked physically (see euroncap2026vta); no published correlation of protocol scores with field crash rates for AEB, only for the older crash-test stars (kullgren2010comparison).
notes: Cost statements from https://www.euroncap.com/faq/ (fetched).

name: Euro NCAP AEB/LSS VRU test protocol
modality: Vehicle driven by path-following robot toward articulated pedestrian (adult/child) and cyclist/motorcycle targets in scenarios CPFA/CPNA/CPNC/CPLA/CBNA etc. at stepped speeds; scored by avoidance/speed reduction; pedestrian AEB since 2016, cyclist since 2018, extended 2020 and 2023.
what_it_measures: Vulnerable-road-user crash avoidance on a proving ground with human surrogates.
size: multiple scenarios x speed steps; runs per scenario per protocol
reported_metrics: Star ratings; see kullgren2010euroncap for real-world validity of Euro NCAP ratings.
cost_evidence: Requires driving robot, guided target platforms, proving ground; no cost figures published.
validity_evidence: Kullgren et al. 2010: 5-star cars have 10% (+/-2.5) lower injury risk, 23% (+/-8) lower fatal/serious, 68% (+/-32) lower fatal risk than 2-star cars (crashworthiness ratings; AEB VRU tests post-date that study).
notes: Protocol PDF (v4.5) returned 404 on both euroncap.com and cdn; the protocols landing page and Wikipedia timeline were fetched. Scenario details from search snippets and prior protocol knowledge.

name: RP2 stop-sign stickers (Robust Physical-World Attacks)
org: University of Michigan / UC Berkeley / University of Washington
modality: Printed black/white sticker perturbations on a real stop sign; classifier fed lab photos (varied distance/angle) and video frames from a moving vehicle; scored by targeted misclassification rate.
what_it_measures: Physical realisability of adversarial examples for road-sign classifiers with an explicit two-stage lab + field protocol.
size: lab image set over distances/angles; drive-by video frames (count not in abstract)
reported_metrics: 100% targeted misclassification in lab; 84.8% of frames in moving-vehicle field test.
cost_evidence: Consumer printer stickers; a car; no figures.
validity_evidence: Lab-vs-field gap (100% vs 84.8%) is itself a validity data point for lab tests.

name: Force pain thresholds for ISO/TS 15066 collision limits
org: KIRO / Fraunhofer IFF / Kyung Hee Univ.
modality: Pendulum impactor with force/torque sensing (10 kHz) strikes deltoid and thigh of 37 male subjects with wedge (R5) and cylindrical (R40) impactors; pain thresholds compared to ISO/TS 15066 biomechanical limits.
what_it_measures: Empirical basis for power-and-force-limiting collision limits used in cobot collision tests.
reported_metrics: Third-quartile force pain thresholds ~121-310 N depending on impactor and body region.
cost_evidence: Human-subject study; instrumented pendulum rig; no cost stated.
validity_evidence: Direct human pain measurement; notes most ISO/TS 15066 limits are preliminary literature-derived values.
notes: Represents the standards-based contact-test layer (ISO/TS 15066 PFL with biofidelic measuring devices).

name: IIHS Vehicle-to-Vehicle Front Crash Prevention 2.0 test protocol
modality: Vehicle approaches stationary Soft Car 360 GVT, a motorcycle surrogate, or a real dry-van trailer at 50, 60 and 70 km/h, centred and offset; scored on FCW timing and speed reduction; rated good/acceptable/marginal/poor.
what_it_measures: Higher-speed and non-passenger-vehicle front crash prevention, replacing the 2013-2022 test at 20 and 40 km/h.
reported_metrics: Old 20/40 km/h scenarios covered <3% of police-reported front-to-rear crashes; new speeds and targets raise relevance to 36% of rear-end and 43% of fatal rear-end crashes (Kidd 2022); AEB reduces police-reported front-to-rear crashes 34-50% across studies.
cost_evidence: Requires GVT Rev F, motorcycle surrogate and a real tractor trailer; covered track for night tests; brake conditioning runs before each session.
validity_evidence: Protocol redesign explicitly driven by level-9 evidence that superior-rated systems still under-perform against trucks and motorcycles (iihs2023trucks).

name: IIHS Pedestrian AEB test protocol (Version IV)
modality: Production vehicle driven at 20/40 km/h (perpendicular adult and child, child emerging from behind parked cars) and 40/60 km/h (parallel adult) toward articulated pedestrian dummies on a 4activeSB surfboard platform; day and night; 3 valid runs per speed and lighting condition; scored by speed reduction/avoidance into good/acceptable/marginal/poor.
what_it_measures: Pedestrian AEB crash avoidance/mitigation on a closed track with human surrogates.
size: 3 scenarios x 2 speeds x 2 lighting x 3 runs = 36 runs per vehicle (plus brake conditioning)
reported_metrics: Ratings per vehicle; HLDI real-world: pedestrian AEB cut pedestrian-related claim frequency 35% (Subaru EyeSight) and ~27% in a later analysis; ~32-33% crash reduction in daylight/lit roads, none in unlit dark.
cost_evidence: Per vehicle: 36 scored runs plus 16 brake-conditioning stops, dummy targets, surfboard platform, instrumented track; dollar cost not stated.
validity_evidence: HLDI insurance-claim analyses show systems that pass these tests reduce real pedestrian claims 27-35%; IIHS notes no benefit in unlit conditions, motivating the night test.
notes: Protocol PDF fetched and text-extracted; HLDI numbers from IIHS news page (fetched).

name: FMVSS No. 127 Automatic Emergency Braking rule (May 2024, amended Nov 2024)
modality: Compliance track tests of the production vehicle: three lead-vehicle scenarios (stopped, decelerating, slower-moving) at 10-100 km/h and four pedestrian scenarios (crossing, alongside, standing, obstructed) at 10-73 km/h in daylight and darkness, two false-activation tests (steel trench plate, parked vehicles); pass = no contact with the test device in every run; FCW audible and visual signal required up to 145 km/h.
what_it_measures: Regulatory minimum AEB/PAEB/FCW performance for all new light vehicles from 1 Sept 2029.
size: 7 crash-imminent scenarios plus 2 false-activation scenarios; multiple speeds each
reported_metrics: Estimated 362 lives saved and 24,321 non-fatal injuries mitigated per year; benefits 17-21x costs.
cost_evidence: Total annual compliance cost about $354M (2020 dollars), mostly software, radar added on ~5% of fleet; $550k-$680k per life saved; lifetime net benefit $5.82-7.26B. Nov 2024 amendment rejected allowing 5-of-7 run passes and rejected 10 km/h contact tolerance; PAEB no-contact worth about $179.1M vs allowing low-speed contact. Test-house note: high-speed runs need 200-300 m additional track and driving robots, soft targets and launch platforms.
validity_evidence: Benefit estimates derive from real-world effectiveness studies of existing AEB (cicchino2018gm and others), i.e. level-9 evidence is used to justify a level-8 test; no direct validation of the test's own predictive power.
notes: Both the May 2024 rule and Nov 2024 amendment fetched from govinfo. The Final Regulatory Impact Analysis PDF (regulations.gov) returned 403.

name: Embodied AI with Two Arms: zero-shot learning, safety and modularity
modality: Language-instructed bimanual system (LLM planner, VLM perception, point-cloud grasping, real-time trajectory optimizer with compliant tracking) evaluated on sorting, bottle opening and trash disposal with humans in proximity.
what_it_measures: Task success of a modular zero-shot bimanual system and its safe operation near humans via constrained trajectory optimization and compliance.
reported_metrics: none stated in abstract
validity_evidence: none stated
notes: Safety-paper nomination at IROS 2024, but it is a system paper: the evaluation protocol is not a reusable safety benchmark. Included as adjacent only; do not cite as an eval.

name: METR developer productivity RCT
modality: Randomised controlled trial: 16 experienced open-source developers, 246 real issues randomly assigned AI-allowed vs not; outcome = completion time.
what_it_measures: Real-world impact of AI tools on expert developer productivity (a level-9 ground truth against which benchmark claims can be checked).
reported_metrics: 19% slowdown with AI; developers predicted 20% speedup, experts 38-39%.
cost_evidence: Developers paid for real work (rate not in abstract); 246 tasks of real repository work.
validity_evidence: Direct demonstration that benchmark-style capability does not translate to real productivity; 20 robustness checks.

name: Efficient quantitative validation of residual risk (FOT reduction approaches)
modality: Systematic evaluation of reduction approaches for Field Operational Testing (FOT) against quantifiability, validity threats, missing links and black-box compatibility.
what_it_measures: Whether any method can replace on-road exposure for demonstrating residual risk at higher automation levels.
reported_metrics: Conclusion: no identified alternative can fully replace FOT.
cost_evidence: Frames FOT effort as impractical at higher automation levels; no numbers in abstract.
validity_evidence: Catalogues validity threats of each substitute for on-road testing.

name: Initial Indications of Safety of Driverless ADS (SF crash rates)
modality: Crashes per million miles from public reports: Uber TNC (CPUC 2020), supervised AVs (CA DMV Dec 2020-Nov 2022), driverless Waymo and Cruise (Mar 2022-Aug 2023), San Francisco excluding freeways.
what_it_measures: Independent (non-company) comparison of driverless and supervised AV crash rates to a human ride-hail baseline.
reported_metrics: Supervised AV about equal to Uber human CPMM; driverless Waymo lower; driverless Cruise higher; samples judged too small for firm conclusions.
validity_evidence: Highlights that outcome comparisons depend heavily on the baseline and on sample size.

name: Confidence intervals for rare-event rate estimation with importance sampling (AV)
org: Waymo/Google statisticians (affiliation not shown on abstract page)
modality: Compound-Poisson model with Horvitz-Thompson estimation for event rates from importance-sampled AV logs; exponential-bootstrap CIs with monotonicity guarantee and saddlepoint implementation.
what_it_measures: How to put valid confidence intervals on rare-event rates (collisions per million miles) when data are sampled non-uniformly.
reported_metrics: Method paper; accepted at Annals of Applied Statistics.
cost_evidence: Motivated by rarity: collisions once per several million human miles.
validity_evidence: Statistical validity results; no outcome comparison.
notes: Affiliation inferred (Chamandy, Hohnhold are known Google/Waymo statisticians); not confirmed on the page.

name: Real-world effects of GM Forward Collision Alert and Front Automatic Braking
modality: Poisson regression of police-reported rear-end striking crash involvement rates, MY2013-2015 GM vehicles with vs without optional systems (VIN-matched), controlling for known risk factors.
what_it_measures: Crash-rate reduction attributable to FCW alone and FCW+AEB.
reported_metrics: AEB+FCW: 43% fewer rear-end striking crashes, 64% fewer with injuries, 68% fewer with third-party injuries; FCW alone: 17%, 30%, 32%.
validity_evidence: Level-9 outcome evidence that the technology class evaluated by track protocols delivers real reductions; consistent with 27-50% reductions in Volvo/Mazda and multi-make studies cited in the paper.

name: Characteristics of rear-end crashes involving AEB-equipped vehicles
modality: Logistic regression on rear-end crashes from 23 US states (2009-2016) to find situations where AEB-equipped striking vehicles are overrepresented.
what_it_measures: Residual crash scenarios that AEB fails to prevent.
reported_metrics: AEB-equipped vehicles overrepresented in crashes with turning lead vehicles, lane changes, non-passenger-vehicle partners, snow/ice and higher-speed roads.
validity_evidence: Shows the test scenarios (stationary target, low speed) miss the residual crash population; motivated the 2024 IIHS protocol change.
notes: Publisher page returned 403; verified via Semantic Scholar API record.

name: Effects of pedestrian AEB on pedestrian crash risk
modality: Poisson regression and quasi-induced exposure comparing pedestrian crash rates per insured vehicle year for vehicles with and without optional pedestrian AEB.
what_it_measures: Real-world effectiveness of pedestrian AEB by lighting, speed limit and manoeuvre.
reported_metrics: 25-27% fewer pedestrian crashes, 29-30% fewer pedestrian injury crashes; no evidence of effect in unlit darkness, at speed limits >= 50 mph, or while turning.
validity_evidence: Directly exposes the domain where daytime track tests overstate protection; led to IIHS night testing (iihs2024paeb) and FMVSS 127 darkness tests.

name: Cruise Oct 2023 pedestrian incident and aftermath
modality: Operational incident record: driverless vehicle struck and dragged a pedestrian ~20 ft after a hit-and-run; DMV permit suspension (24 Oct 2023), recall of 950 vehicles (8 Nov 2023), Quinn Emanuel/Exponent review (Jan 2024), USD 1.5M NHTSA fine (Sep 2024).
what_it_measures: A single rare deployment event and its regulatory consequence; demonstrates the asymmetric value of level-9 evidence.
reported_metrics: Permit suspension, 950-vehicle recall, USD 1.5M fine.
cost_evidence: Illustrates the cost of a missed failure mode (fleet grounded) rather than evaluation cost.
validity_evidence: Shows aggregate crash-rate benchmarks published a week earlier did not capture the failure mode.
notes: Secondary source; cite the Quinn Emanuel report or DMV order directly in the paper if possible.

name: Waymo vs human liability claims (Swiss Re, 3.8M rider-only miles)
modality: Insurance liability claims frequency (bodily injury, property damage) of the Waymo fleet versus Swiss Re private-passenger baselines calibrated by mileage and zip code.
what_it_measures: Claims per million miles as a third-party safety outcome metric.
size: 3.8M rider-only miles plus 35M+ miles with a safety specialist
reported_metrics: Rider-only: 0 bodily-injury claims vs 1.11 per million miles baseline; property damage 0.78 vs 3.26 per million miles.
cost_evidence: Uses existing insurer claims infrastructure; no evaluation cost beyond deployment.
validity_evidence: Claims are an independent, financially incentivised outcome record; small counts limit precision.

name: Waymo vs latest-generation human-driven vehicles: liability claims at 25.3M miles
modality: Liability claims frequency over 25.3M rider-only miles versus Swiss Re baselines from 500k+ claims and 200B+ miles, including a 2018-2021 ADAS-equipped vehicle cohort.
what_it_measures: Property-damage and bodily-injury claim reductions vs overall population and vs new ADAS-equipped vehicles.
size: 25.3M miles; 9 property damage claims, 2 bodily injury claims
reported_metrics: 88% fewer PD and 92% fewer BI claims vs overall population; 86% and 90% vs 2018-2021 ADAS-equipped vehicles; expected human counts 78 PD and 26 BI.
validity_evidence: Independent insurer data; both BI claims still open at publication.
notes: Only the Waymo blog post was fetched; author list from the blog's citation, not the paper page.

name: AV disengagements: trends, triggers and regulatory limitations
modality: Analysis of California DMV disengagement reports 2014-2017: frequencies, miles per disengagement, triggers and contributory factors.
what_it_measures: Reliability trends of supervised AV testing and the limits of disengagement reporting as a safety metric.
reported_metrics: Environmental contributors about 10.8% of disengagements (poor lane markings 4.63%, construction 2.20%, pedestrians 2.03%, weather 0.69%) from search summary.
validity_evidence: Documents inconsistent reporting across manufacturers, undermining disengagements as a comparable safety proxy.
notes: ScienceDirect returned 403; not fetched. Included because it is the standard citation on disengagement-report validity.

name: Interpreting Safety Outcomes (Waymo credibility paradox)
modality: Argument paper: observed contact events during fully autonomous operation vs human baselines, framed within a broader readiness determination.
what_it_measures: How much confidence lagging outcome statistics can carry early in deployment and why they must be complemented by other estimation techniques.
reported_metrics: none stated
validity_evidence: Names the 'credibility paradox': outcome data are the most credible but least available; argues for event-level analysis and continuous confidence updating.

name: Cruise/UMTRI human ridehail crash benchmark (San Francisco)
modality: 5.6M miles of human ridehail driving (fleet telematics + instrumented vehicles) over 2 years in SF, excluding >35 mph roads, to build a crash-rate benchmark; Cruise fleet crash rates compared.
what_it_measures: Human benchmark for urban ridehail crashes and an ADS comparison.
reported_metrics: Human benchmark ~64.9 crashes per million miles (1 per 15,414 mi); Cruise reported 65% fewer collisions overall, 94% fewer as primary contributor, 74% fewer with meaningful injury risk.
cost_evidence: Two-year, multi-institution instrumented study to build the benchmark alone.
validity_evidence: Cautionary: published one week before the Oct 2, 2023 pedestrian-dragging incident that led to permit suspension (see cruise2023incident).
notes: Primary technical report not fetched; press release verified.

name: Characterization and mitigation of functional insufficiencies in ADS
modality: Categorisation of 2021 California DMV disengagements and 10+ hours of road-test video into functional insufficiencies (world model, motion planning, traffic rules, ODD) vs system faults; proposes the Daruma multi-channel architecture.
what_it_measures: Share of field disengagements due to SOTIF-type insufficiencies vs ISO 26262-type faults.
reported_metrics: Disengagements are five times more often caused by functional insufficiencies than by system faults.
validity_evidence: Field evidence that SOTIF-style (level 3-5 scenario) testing targets the dominant failure class.

name: IIHS: front crash prevention less effective against trucks and motorcycles
modality: Crash-data effectiveness by struck-vehicle type plus track tests of five superior-rated vehicles against truck and motorcycle targets.
what_it_measures: Gap between a top track rating and field effectiveness by partner type.
reported_metrics: Rear-end crash reductions: 53% vs passenger vehicles, 38% vs medium/heavy trucks, 41% vs motorcycles; all five test vehicles were 'superior' in the old test yet alerted later for trucks and motorcycles.
validity_evidence: Direct evidence that a saturated level-8 rating (everyone superior) stopped discriminating field performance; the 2024 protocol (50/60/70 km/h, new targets) was the response.

name: RAND Driving to Safety (miles to demonstrate reliability)
modality: Statistical analysis (binomial / Poisson confidence bounds) of on-road miles needed to bound AV failure rates; no system under test, the 'evaluation' is naturalistic driving exposure.
what_it_measures: Miles of failure-free or observed driving needed to demonstrate fatality, injury and crash rates relative to human baselines at given confidence and precision.
size: US 2013 baselines: 1.09 fatalities, 77 injuries, 190 crashes per 100M miles
reported_metrics: 275M failure-free miles to show fatality rate <= 1.09/100M miles at 95% confidence (about 12.5 years for a 100-vehicle fleet 24/7 at 25 mph); about 8.8B miles (about 400 years) to demonstrate a 20% improvement over the human fatality rate.
cost_evidence: Time cost only: tens to hundreds of years of fleet driving; motivates accelerated, virtual and scenario testing.
validity_evidence: Level-9 outcome statistics are the ground truth against which every other level is compared; the paper quantifies why they are unattainable pre-deployment.
notes: Outside the 2018-2026 window but canonical. rand.org returned HTTP 403; verified via the autosafety.org mirror of the PDF. Pre-2018 but canonical; PDF fetched and text-extracted (rand.org blocked). Aliases in sweeps: kalra2016drivingtosafety.

name: Safety argument for public-road testing of AVs
modality: Safety-case structure for human-supervised road testing: supervisor alertness and timely response, adequate failure management, and an autonomy failure profile compatible with supervision.
what_it_measures: Conditions under which level-9 data collection with safety drivers is itself acceptably safe.
reported_metrics: none stated
validity_evidence: Key claim: supervisability degrades nonlinearly as autonomy failure rates fall, so safer systems are harder to supervise.

name: Positive Trust Balance for self-driving car deployment
modality: Decision framework: deploy on a practicable amount of testing plus engineering rigour and safety culture, conditioned on stringent post-deployment SPI feedback.
what_it_measures: How to decide deployment when lagging outcome metrics are statistically insufficient.
reported_metrics: none stated
validity_evidence: Explicitly trades pre-deployment confidence for operational monitoring; a VOI-style argument in prose.

name: Euro NCAP star ratings vs real-world crash data
modality: Paired-comparison of two-car crashes (controls for crash severity) and police/insurance injury data, grouped by Euro NCAP star rating.
what_it_measures: Whether the crash-test star rating predicts real injury and fatality risk.
reported_metrics: Later Kullgren et al. (2019, ESV) update: 5-star cars have 10% +/- 2.5% lower injury risk than 2-star cars, 23 +/- 8% lower fatal/serious, 68 +/- 32% lower fatal (from search summary of the 2019 paper).
validity_evidence: The best-documented case in automotive testing of a standardized physical test correlating with outcomes; note it concerns crashworthiness stars, not AEB.

Pre-2018 but the canonical track-test-to-outcome validity study. tandfonline/PubMed blocked; metadata verified via Semantic Scholar API; numbers from search snippet of the abstract. name: Waymo rider-only crash rates vs human benchmarks (7.1M miles)
modality: Retrospective observational comparison: NHTSA Standing General Order (SGO) crash reports plus company mileage versus human benchmarks matched on vehicle type, road type and geography.
what_it_measures: Incidents per million miles (IPMM) for any-injury-reported and police-reported crashes, ADS vs human.
size: 7.14M rider-only miles (Phoenix, SF, LA) through Oct 2023
reported_metrics: Any-injury 0.6 vs 2.80 IPMM (80% reduction); police-reported 2.1 vs 4.68 IPMM (55% reduction); statistically significant when pooled.
cost_evidence: Requires millions of deployed miles; authors caution results are 'directional'.
validity_evidence: Ground-truth outcome data; caveats on benchmark imprecision and human underreporting.
notes: Aliases in sweeps: kusano2023waymo7m.

name: Waymo rider-only crash rates by crash type (56.7M miles)
modality: As kusano2023comparison, disaggregated into 11 crash-type groups; SGO data through Jan 2025.
what_it_measures: Crashed-vehicle rates for injury-reported and airbag-deployment crashes by crash type versus matched human benchmarks.
reported_metrics: Vehicle-to-vehicle intersection crashes: 96% reduction in injury-reported (CI 87-99%) and 91% in airbag-deployment (CI 76-98%); significant reductions for cyclist, motorcycle, pedestrian and single-vehicle groups; no significant disbenefit in any of 11 groups.
cost_evidence: Tens of millions of deployed miles needed before per-type confidence intervals become informative.
validity_evidence: Outcome data; the paper is the empirical anchor for what lower-level evaluations should predict.
notes: Aliases in sweeps: kusano2025waymo56m.

name: NHTSA Standing General Order 2021-01 crash reporting
modality: Mandatory reporting of crashes involving ADS and L2 ADAS vehicles by manufacturers/operators to NHTSA; public incident-report datasets released periodically.

reported_metrics: none (regulatory instrument)

validity_evidence: Known issues: narrative redactions (Tesla until 2026), reporting-threshold differences vs police data.

name: On the safety of mobile robots in public spaces: gaps in EN ISO 13482
modality: Standards gap analysis for personal-care/service robots deployed among pedestrians: crowds, social norms and proxemics, and people's misbehaviour are not covered by ISO 13482:2014 certification.

name: Unsupervised anomaly detection for self-flying delivery drones
modality: Flight logs (control inputs + sensor readings) of hybrid aerial delivery vehicles; robust regression fits nominal flight dynamics while discarding contaminated missions; anomalies scored against injected and real anomaly types (3-sigma thresholds, turbulence, equipment faults) by detection rate.
what_it_measures: Whether a runtime/offline monitor can flag abnormal missions in a real drone fleet without labelled failures, under heavy training-set contamination.
reported_metrics: High detection rates across anomaly types (exact figures not in abstract).
cost_evidence: Real fleet flight data at scale; no labelling required (unsupervised).
validity_evidence: Evaluated on real flight logs including real equipment anomalies.

name: Diversity analysis of lead-vehicle safety metrics
org: Transportation Research Center / Ohio State / NHTSA
modality: 33 base metrics (51 variants) from 1967-2022 applied to highway trajectory data and to a high-risk collision/near-miss dataset; agreement between metrics examined.

size: 33 base metrics, up to 51 variants; two datasets

validity_evidence: Direct evidence that the scoring choice, not just the test level, changes verdicts; a false-alarm / sensitivity concern for any metric-based evaluation.

name: Amazon robotic vs non-robotic warehouse serious injury rates (SOC report)
modality: OSHA Form 300A injury logs by facility, split by robotic vs non-robotic fulfilment centres; serious (lost-time/restricted) injury rate per 100 workers.

cost_evidence: Uses mandatory OSHA reporting; no evaluation cost.
validity_evidence: Observational; confounded by throughput/pace; but it is direct level-9 harm data for a robot fleet.

modality: Framework proposing ethical black-box logging and aviation-style investigation processes for social-robot accidents.

modality: NLP and transfer learning over 2014-2020 California DMV disengagement reports.

validity_evidence: Human-initiated disengagements dominate, so the metric measures driver judgement as much as system failure.

name: Planning Reliability Assurance Tests for AVs
modality: Statistical test planning: how many AVs to test for how many miles and the pass criterion, using homogeneous and non-homogeneous Poisson process models fitted to California DMV disengagement data; Pareto-front trade-off of test objectives.
what_it_measures: Required test fleet size, mileage and pass/fail rule for a reliability demonstration test given disengagement-rate priors.
reported_metrics: none stated

validity_evidence: Uses disengagements as the reliability proxy; validity of disengagements as a safety proxy is itself contested (see fu2024insufficiencies, zhang2021disengagement).

name: Anthropic Responsible Scaling Policy (v3.4)
modality: Policy: capability thresholds (CBRN, AI R&D automation/acceleration) checked by comprehensive assessments; ASL-3/4 deployment and security standards.
what_it_measures: Deployment gate: thresholds trigger safeguards; comprehensive assessment every 6 months (was 3) to allow higher-quality elicitation.
reported_metrics: v3.4 effective 8 Jul 2026; Opus 4 uplift trial threshold 2.8x/5x; sabotage risk reports for models exceeding prior capability.
cost_evidence: Assessment cadence lengthened explicitly to afford better elicitation; policy admits past evals lacked basic elicitation (best-of-N, CoT).
validity_evidence: Acknowledged under-elicitation gaps now tracked.

name: Reachability-based analysis of online-adapting human models
modality: The robot's online learning algorithm for a parameterized human model is treated as a dynamical system whose control is the human data; dynamic programming computes the set of hypotheses learnable in finite time and best/worst-case learning times; scored analytically, no real data.
what_it_measures: Safety-relevant properties of a human predictor: what it could learn online, how fast (worst/best case), and which initializations guarantee finite-time convergence; applied to driving intersection, confidence-aware navigation, legible/deceptive navigation, gradient-based reward learning.
size: 4 simulated domains; low-dimensional parameter spaces only.
reported_metrics: Driving: correct branching time cuts distance-to-goal 6.88 m to 3.42 m while safe; confidence-detection best-case 0.9-2.72 s; learning time <=2.2 s vs ~4.7 s by initialization.
cost_evidence: Dynamic programming over discrete or 2D continuous parameter spaces; does not scale beyond low dimensions.
validity_evidence: none stated; no real human data.
notes: Code https://github.com/abajcsy/pred_analyzer fetched (200). An offline verification/analysis tool rather than an empirical eval. Level set to None on the 0-9 ladder (analytical reachability tool, no system evaluated; sweeps had 1).

modality: Text-to-image models (SD 1.5/2.1, PixArt, Kandinsky); 32k-concept archetypal SAE on DINOv2 features compares concept prevalence in real vs generated images

name: Human-centered utility benchmark for attribution methods (Meta-predictor)
modality: Image classifier + attribution heatmaps shown to crowdworkers; scored by 'Utility' = AUC of how much explanations improve humans' ability to predict the model's decisions vs no-explanation baseline
what_it_measures: Whether explanation methods actually help humans understand a model in three scenarios (bias detection, expert strategy, failure cases), and whether standard faithfulness metrics (Deletion) predict that usefulness.
size: n=1150 AMT participants (240-242 retained per scenario after screening), 6 attribution methods, 3 datasets (Husky vs Wolf, Leaves, ImageNet)
reported_metrics: Grad-CAM (p<0.001), Occlusion (p=0.01), SmoothGrad (p=0.034) significantly useful for bias detection; no method useful on ImageNet; faithfulness (1-Deletion) shows no positive correlation with human utility, if anything anti-correlated; strong correlation with perceptual similarity and explanation complexity
cost_evidence: 1150 paid crowdworkers via Amazon Mechanical Turk; ~30 subjects per condition
validity_evidence: Direct human-in-the-loop measurement; key finding is that proxy metrics do NOT predict human-measured value
notes: Not embodied. Directly relevant to a value-of-information argument: shows cheap proxy metrics can have zero or negative information about the quantity that matters. Venue NeurIPS 2022 from memory of proceedings; arXiv v3 Jan 2023.

name: Psychophysical comparison of neuron vs dictionary bases

reported_metrics: Dictionary-based representations consistently rated more interpretable than neurons (effect sizes in paper)
validity_evidence: Human ratings are the target quantity; no downstream task validation
notes: Human-labelling cost example for evaluating interpretability tools.

name: Controlled evaluation of SAE architectures (MP-SAE)

validity_evidence: Ground-truth features known by construction
